In short

  • What's bad: 67 items still fail. About 66% of them fail in two places: our executor code (23) and the planner's reasoning (21). Only 7 are the free models' fault, and 8 aren't real failures (grader or test wrong).
  • When the plan was fine but our code broke it (23 items), the plan that ran already scored 4.22 of 5. Claude's plan scored no better (4.04). Thinking harder can't fix these; the code has to.
  • When the agent's reasoning was wrong (21 items), Claude is clearly better: 4.29 vs 3.43 for what ran. The agent at high effort only reached 3.62. The gap is knowledge, not effort: Claude opened the materials and knew what our code does with each setting.
  • Across all 67 items, Claude did better, not dramatically: 4.01 vs 3.69. Its plan was better on 22, the same on 31, and worse on 14. Claude expects 62 of 67 to pass once its named fix is in (6 certain, 56 likely, 5 unlikely).

How the harness works, and is it too restrictive?

  1. Sheet (LLM). One call reads the conversation into a fixed set of fields for the goal (size, style, words, length…). Each field is stated, inferred or unknown. Code turns unknown or low-confidence fields into questions, up to 4. This is the only place the agent is challenged structurally.
  2. Planner (LLM). One call gets the sheet, the material file names, the session's assets and the tool catalogue. It writes the whole tree: each step's tool, inputs, output name, prompt and a free-text "extra".
  3. price / guard (code). Picks the model per step (qwen for lettering or faithful edits), then patches a few known mistakes (transparency, a missing style).
  4. Executor (code). Runs the steps in order. It checks only that each input exists. Then it post-processes: crop or pad to the aspect, drop clip audio, read the lettering back and fix it once.

Not too restrictive; too trusting. The agent is asked what to do, and the tree is run as written. Nothing pushes back on it:

  • A setting a tool can't do is silently ignored, and the step still reports "done". Examples: "dissolve" or "5 s then 3 s" to assemble, "navy, left-aligned" to text-overlay, "8 seconds" to voice.
  • The agent never sees the materials, only their names. It can't know a clip is silent or where a speaker changes.
  • Outputs aren't checked against what the step was for, except lettering. A wrong picture flows into the next step.
  • Until today, the planner didn't receive the user's own style and palette words (fixed).

Where it is restrictive, it's a few absolute planner rules. For example, "never a picture plus a text-overlay for the same design" stopped the right split on a flyer with a long address (A03d). As asked, I'm not adding gates now; this page shows which stage broke so we can decide later.

Long Venue Address Preserved Exactly

31

Please make a clean black-and-cream 4:5 flyer. Text: "Printmakers' Open Studio", "9 October 2027", "11:00–17:00", and "Unit 14B, Second Floor, The Old Foundry Arts Centre, 127–129 St. John's Road, Kingston upon Thames, KT1 2AB". Keep that whole address letter for letter, including punctuation—wrap it over lines if needed, but don't shorten it. No extra words.

broke at: Executor lettering read-back + model-limit + agent-reasoning Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent trusted the catalogue line 'lettering: true GUARANTEES designed lettering spelled exactly' and put the whole 108-character address in as ONE quoted string, in a single qwen render at 1:1 then a centre crop. It gave no size hierarchy or line plan for the address, and it dropped the user's 'black-and-cream' from the prompt (the planner prompt even uses 'black and cream' as its example of user words to keep). I treat a 108-character address as small print that a 640 px diffusion model will not spell reliably. I would let qwen letter only the three short lines, which it got right in both renders, and set the address with the one tool that guarantees exact characters: text-overlay, by code. The agent could not choose that split. The planner rule says 'One node per designed piece; never a picture node plus a text-overlay for the same design', the WORDS rule sends every flyer word to lettering:true, and nothing in the catalogue says lettering degrades with string length. What sank the output was the harness. Its single fix told qwen to letter the address while also deleting the 'Third address line' and 'Fourth address line' entirely. The fix broke the two lines that had been correct, nothing re-read the result, and the node was marked done with the note 'lettering fixed'.

evidence from the files
flyer_4x5.png (512x640, centre-cut from a 640x640 qwen render): headline, date and time are correct, with a curly ’ in Printmakers’. The address reads 'Unit 14B, Secomd' / 'Floor, [garbled] Arts Centre,' / '127–129 St. John’s Road' (no comma after Road) / 'Kingston  upon Thames, KT1 2AB'. The background is near-white rather than cream. flyer_source-before-text-fix.png is the first render: huge type filling the square, address lines 'Unit 14B, Second' and 'Floor, The Old Foundry Arts' correct, the remaining three lines garbled. exec.json shows the fix prompt asking qwen to letter the whole address and also to 'remove the Third address line … entirely … remove the Fourth address line … entirely … the people, faces, poses, hands … stay'. The fixed image shrank the block and broke lines 1–2. execute.js runs no readback after fixText. The judge was right overall (the address is garbled); faulting the curly apostrophe is over-strict typographically but did not change the verdict.

Fix (1) Harness, the lettering readback in execute.js and buildable.js: a garbled rendering of a WANTED string is a misspelling, never a 'stray' to remove. Fix one quoted line per edit, naming its position. Re-read after every fix, up to 2 rounds, and set the node 'flagged: lettering still wrong' instead of 'done / lettering fixed' when it still misreads. Drop fixText's hard-coded aspect_ratio 16:9 and its 'people, faces, poses, hands' wording for designs. (2) text-overlay: honour extra 'color: #hex; box: none; size: N' (the file header already promises 'box') so long exact text can be set in a design's own colours. (3) Planner rule and catalogue line: exact text over about 40 characters (an address, small print, terms) on a design is lettered by code. The image letters the short headline lines and leaves an empty zone, and text-overlay sets the long text, as a named exception to 'never a picture node plus a text-overlay'.

A06c

Transparent Moon Bakery Logo

17

Make a square logo for my bakery, Mooncrumb: a gold crescent moon above dark navy lettering. Send it as a transparent PNG so I can put it on different backgrounds. No white box behind it.

broke at: Executor planner rules + agent-reasoning + wrong-tool + model-limit + grader Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent's own plan was a single qwen image step; it ignored 'transparent PNG ... no white box' entirely and did not ask the image for a plain keyable ground. The code guard in plan.js then appended background-remove (the catalogue's TRANSPARENT rule and its 'WELL: a transparent PNG: a logo' line point there). That AI cutter is a salient-object segmenter: it kept the crescent and treated the word 'Mooncrumb' as background, deleting it. I would make the logo flat on pure white and key the white out by code (filter look: transparent, which exists in the harness but is not mentioned on filter's catalogue line), so every mark, including the lettering, is kept. The agent could not have chosen filter from what it saw: its line lists only bw/sepia/warm/cool/bright/dark/contrast.

evidence from the files
mooncrumb-logo.png (qwen, 640x640) is a clean, correctly spelled logo: gold crescent above navy serif 'Mooncrumb' on near-white (250,250,250). mooncrumb-logo-transparent.png has alpha 0 on 397,979 of 409,600 pixels and every visible pixel lies in rows 160-360 (the crescent); the lettering rows (~370-450) are fully transparent, so background-remove erased the name. The RGB hidden under alpha 0 is gold (190,153,95), which is why the judge, whose input path drops alpha, described a 'tan square' with a 'faint crescent': the background really is transparent, but the fail is still right because the name is gone. Running the harness's own colorkey (0xfafafa:0.12:0.08) on mooncrumb-logo.png in memory keeps 23,097 opaque pixels including 8,468 in the lettering rows, with only 506 semi-transparent edge pixels.

Fix 1) Catalogue: on filter add 'transparent: keys out the plain background of a flat design (logo, icon, sticker, lettering) into a true-alpha PNG, every mark kept'; on background-remove change WELL to 'a photographed product or person' and add CANNOT 'logos or designs with words: it erases the lettering'; change the CHOOSING rule to 'TRANSPARENT: a design made here -> image on plain pure white (say so in the prompt), then filter look: transparent; a photo subject -> background-remove'. 2) Keep the post-run plan.js guard that routes a lettered last step to filter, and extend it to any logo/icon/sticker/flat-vector image even without lettering, and have it append 'isolated on plain pure white, flat colours, no shadow' to that image prompt. 3) Grader: composite RGBA outputs over a checkerboard and a dark colour before sending them to the judge and report alpha coverage; it read alpha-0 pixels as a tan opaque square and would read a correctly keyed logo as a 'white box'.

Three Distinct Cycling Logo Options

52

Give me three different logo options for my cycling club, Moss & Mile. Simple green and black on white, each with the name and a small symbol. Your call on the symbols, but make them genuinely different ideas. Three separate square images please, not a collage.

broke at: Executor planner rules Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent's three prompts are good on everything they mention: qwen with lettering, the exact name with the ampersand, one standalone mark each, and three genuinely different ideas (wheel, winding route, MM monogram) with different layouts. None of them says green, black or white, so qwen drew a clean black-on-white logo three times. The planner never saw the palette: the sheet filled direction with the enum value "stated" and kept "Simple green and black on white" only in that field's quote, and plan.js builds the SHEET lines as `field: value (source)`, so the planner read `direction: stated (stated)`. Its desired_state confirms it ("...each featuring the exact name and a small, genuinely different symbol"), and the planner's own rule "THE USER'S WORDS ARE THE SPEC ... 'green and black on white' is green, black and pure white" could not fire on words it was never shown. I would lead every prompt with the palette and say which part is which colour (the symbol green, the name black, the ground pure white), because qwen defaults to monochrome for a "clean logo".

evidence from the files
I opened all three PNGs (640x640). The wheel sits above the name, the two-line name has a thin S-route beside it, and the MM sits above a serif name. All three are pure black on near-white with no green, and 'Moss & Mile' is spelled correctly in each. In session.json the sheet has direction value 'stated' and quote 'Simple green and black on white, each with the name and a small symbol.'. The plan's desired_state has no palette, and none of the three prompts names a colour. The judge is right.

Fix Carry the user's look into the planner. In plan.js print each stated field's quote next to its value (e.g. `direction: stated — "Simple green and black on white"`), or in sheet.js fill `style` whenever direction=stated, not only when direction=needed. Extend guard() in plan.js so every colour word in the stated direction quote must appear in every image/image-edit prompt (prepend "In green and black on pure white:" when it is missing). The same lost-quote path dropped "watercolor" in D22b and "soft watercolours" in J50a.

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

No real divergence. The agent read the request right (one supplied photo, recolour only the hatchback, keep the rest). It picked image-edit with fidelity on, so it ran on qwen, and it said what must stay. The catalogue's own note ('navy came out teal' on klein) is why qwen was the right model. My only change would be the prompt: 'the red car' is ambiguous because there is a second red car parked in the background. I would name 'the red hatchback in the foreground', ask for a deep navy, say the background car stays red, and forbid moving or reframing anything. The failure is in the editor itself. qwen redraws the whole frame and adds a small geometric warp: about a 1.7% horizontal squeeze plus a 3 px shift, with no vertical change. That moves the rear bumper, the plate and the parked cars on the right. The catalogue says plainly that image-edit cannot leave the rest pixel-identical, and no catalogue tool can merge the recoloured body back into the untouched original. The agent could not have reached 'the rest unchanged' with these tools.

evidence from the files
Input car-red.jpg and output car-navy.png are both 640x384. The body paint went from about #902B39 to #0A2146 or #0F2443, a true navy, and the background red car stayed red. A pixel diff shows the whole frame re-rendered (mean abs diff 19.8, with tree texture changed everywhere). Block matching shows a pure horizontal squeeze: +3 px at x=14, 0 near x=200, -7 px at x=600, dy=0 on every row. A point that was red bumper at (440,280) is number plate in the output. In side-by-side crops the rear bumper is lower and rounder and the plate is tilted, and the dark parked car on the right sits about 6 px further left with redrawn contours. The judge's two 'no' verdicts are real, though minor. The harness passed no aspect and called no finish(), so the warp comes from the qwen editor endpoint, not our code.

Fix Add a 'keep-rest merge-back' to the harness for image-edits where the sheet says keep_rest=yes and the change is local (a recolour, a removal, an added prop). Step 1: register the edit to the original with a global affine fit (block matching finds this one at once: dx runs from +3 px at the left edge to -7 px at the right, dy is 0). Step 2: build a change mask where chroma or luma moved past a threshold (here the car body), then dilate and feather it. Step 3: paste the aligned edit into the original inside the mask only, so every other pixel is the user's own. A code 'recolour' look on the filter tool would also work: hue-map one colour range inside an anchor box, keeping luminance so reflections survive. It is riskier, because the tail lights and the background red car share the hue. Then change the image-edit CANNOT line to 'pixel-identical outside the change (merge-back by code when keep_rest)'.

Car Photo in Black and White

81

Make this black and white, please. Just remove the colour—don't change anything else or crop it.

broke at: Bench test + grader Claude's fix would pass: yes

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

There is no divergence. The agent chose the code filter (look: bw) on the supplied photo, which is exactly right: grayscale, nothing redrawn, no crop, and the original size kept. The one failed must-have demands '16:9', but the supplied car-red.jpg is 640x384, which is 5:3. It is the free still model's so-called '16:9' (execute.js itself notes 'The free models' 16:9 is 640x384 (5:3)'). Keeping 'the full original composition without cropping' and also making it 16:9 is impossible without adding bars, and the user said 'don't change anything else or crop it'. The judge saw this ('this preserves the user's requested uncropped composition') and still failed the must-have.

evidence from the files
materials/car-red.jpg is 640x384 (ratio 1.667, i.e. 5:3). assets/car-black-and-white.png is 640x384, rgb, and fully neutral grey: the red hatchback, trees, houses, shadows and sky are all in place, pixel-aligned with the original, with no crop. The judge confirmed 3/4 must-haves and failed only the '16:9' one, noting that the 5:3 shape 'preserves the user's requested uncropped composition'. would_pass assumes the spec fix: with the spec corrected this output passes 4/4. Under the current spec, identical output fails the 16:9 must-have again.

Fix Spec and bench fixture, not the agent. car-red.jpg is 640x384 (5:3) because the fixture was made by the free model's '16:9'. Change B10c's spec aspect to '5:3' (or 'original'), and the must-have to 'The full original composition is retained without cropping, in the original shape'. More generally, the bench should measure each fixture's real aspect when writing specs, and the judge prompt should rank 'the user's explicit no-crop' above a spec aspect that the attached file contradicts.

Square Crop Keeps Whole Sneaker

52

Make this wide photo square for an Instagram post. Keep the whole sneaker in view, and don't stretch it or change anything else.

broke at: Planner + harness + spec + missing-tool Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent correctly chose crop with fit: contain (a 5:3 photo whose sneaker spans ~80% of the width cannot be cropped to a square without cutting it). But it explicitly asked for 'a blurred copy of the photo' as the fill, although the user said 'don't ... change anything else' and the catalogue line for crop says to add 'plain' when the user wants nothing added. It defaulted to the decorative option instead of weighing the user's 'change nothing' against the two fills offered. I would fit the whole, unscaled-in-shape photo into the square with plain bands, so every original pixel stays and nothing new or decorative appears.

evidence from the files
product-sneaker.jpg is 640x384 (5:3); the white sneaker spans x~76-582, 507 px, wider than the largest square crop (384), so some fill is unavoidable. product-sneaker-square.png is 640x640: the full original photo scaled to 640 wide in the middle, sneaker intact and unstretched, with 128 px bands above and below that are a heavily blurred, enlarged copy of the cluttered background (bags, cabinet, wall). The judge's other four must-haves were met; the one fail is exactly the blurred bands, a treatment the user ruled out with 'don't change anything else' and the catalogue's 'plain' option avoids.

Fix 1) Planner/catalogue: make 'plain' the default for crop fit: contain whenever the user says don't change anything, keep it as is, nothing added, or gives no fill preference; use the blurred copy only when asked ('blurred background'). Reword the crop line: 'fit: contain fills with plain bands of the photo's edge colour; add blur only when the user asks for it'. 2) Harness (crop.js): with plain, sample the top band's colour from the top edge and the bottom band's from the bottom edge (here 0x95958b above, 0xbbc0c5 floor below) instead of one top-edge colour for both, so the bands continue the wall and floor. 3) Longer term: an outpaint/expand tool that keeps the original pixels and extends wall and floor, the professional answer to 'square without cropping'.

Which Friend Gets My Face

39

Can you put my face from the park selfie onto someone in this beach photo? Just swap one face and leave everything else alone.

broke at: Executor face-swap Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent did what I would do. It asked the one question that mattered (which person, the expected question), took the answer, picked face-swap-photo with the beach photo as the target and the selfie as the face, and wrote "Target only the blonde woman on the right; exclude the bearded man on the left" in extra. No code reads that line. execute.js always calls /v1/face-swap-photo with `face_swap_mode: "all-faces"`, so Magic Hour put her features on both faces: the man kept his beard and hair but got her eyes, brows, nose and mouth. The catalogue's "POORLY: choosing one of several faces" suggested a hint might work. With the current wiring it is a CANNOT, as the face-swap-video line already says. I checked a workaround with today's tools (crop the woman out, swap, then compose the halves back): it fails here because the two faces touch around x=325 of a 640x384 photo and compose rescales and pads each panel, so the seams would show. The swap has to target one face in the API.

evidence from the files
I opened two-friends.jpg (640x384: bearded man on the left, blonde woman on the right, faces almost touching near x=325), portrait-woman.jpg (dark curly hair, park) and the output. In the output the man's face has become feminine: smooth skin and her eyes, brows and mouth under his own beard and hair. The woman's face also changed (darker brows), and the beach and framing are intact. execute.js hard-codes `face_swap_mode: "all-faces"` in the face-swap-photo body. The judge is right: the man's face was altered.

Fix Wire face-swap-photo and face-swap-video with Magic Hour's individual-faces mode. Run face detection on the target, choose the face named in extra ("target face: left|right|largest|n"), and send face_mappings for that face only. If a picture has several faces and no target was given, ask which one. Until this is wired, change the catalogue line to "CANNOT: one face among several: it changes every face" so the planner tells the user instead of delivering a double swap.

Five Second Talking Face Swap

30

Put the face from this portrait onto the woman in the first 5 seconds of the video. Keep the original sound, framing and everything else.

broke at: Planner + spec Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent read 'in the first 5 seconds' as an edit range inside the full 10.1 s video. It read 'keep ... everything else' as 'keep the rest of the timeline', so it trimmed the remainder and spliced it back. The deliverable became a 10.1 s video in which the woman's face switches back to the original at 5 s. An expert would weigh three things. First, a face that changes identity halfway through a clip is never a usable result. Second, 'keep the original sound, framing and everything else' lists properties of the frame (the audio, the framing, the kitchen), not the timeline. Third, video face swap costs about 30 credits a second on the free tier, which explains why a user caps it at 5 s. The deliverable is the first 5 s, swapped. The sheet schema pushed the agent wrong: the change branch only has 'range' (default whole) and 'keep_rest' (default yes), with no notion of 'deliver only that range'. So range=0-5 plus keep_rest=yes became a splice. The planner had no rule against an identity switch mid-clip. Steps 1 and 2 were exactly right: opening-swapped.mp4 was 5.0 s, the face was swapped in every sample, and the original audio was intact. Steps 3 and 4 broke the result.

evidence from the files
talk-one.mp4 is 10.125 s, 858x480, 24 fps, with AAC speech. opening-swapped.mp4 is 5.0 s, 858x480, with audio. Its audio matches the original's first 5 s with a cross-correlation of 0.9994 at 0 ms lag, and its loudness is identical (-14.4 dB mean). Face crops every 0.5 s across 0-5 s show the portrait's features in all 10 samples: dark heavy brows, brown eyes, a younger rounder face. The original woman's face is visibly different, and the hair stays the target's, as a face swap should. The final output talk-one-face-replaced.mp4 is 10.1 s at 1280x720 (upscaled by assemble) and reverts to the original face after 5 s. The judge's length failure and its 'reverts to the original face' failure are both correct.

Fix Two changes. (1) Sheet: add a 'deliver' field to the change branch, either 'whole asset' or 'only the range', inferred from the words. 'Swap the face in the first 5 seconds' means only the range. 'Change only the first 5 seconds and leave the rest' means the whole asset. (2) Planner rule: 'An identity change (face swap, lip-sync, dub) on part of a clip delivers that part alone unless the user says the rest of the clip must stay. Never splice a swapped section back into the unswapped original: the face would change mid-clip. keep_rest means keep the picture's other content (sound, framing, background), not the remainder of the timeline.'

Two Coworkers Two Replacement Faces

0

Swap both faces in this 10-second office clip: the man's face from the man's portrait, and the woman's from the woman's portrait. Keep their voices and the rest of the video unchanged.

broke at: Catalogue + agent-reasoning + spec Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

Given the catalogue, the agent's diagnosis was correct: face-swap-video 'CANNOT: one face among several: it changes every face', and the executor really does hard-code face_swap_mode 'all-faces'. Its dialog was wrong. The expected behaviour was never to ask, yet it asked three near-identical questions. Twice the user answered 'your call', and it still asked again before ending with nothing made. After the first 'your call' it should have stopped asking and either delivered or stated the limit once. My plan differs because the capability exists one layer down. Magic Hour's /v1/face-swap has an 'individual-faces' mode with up to 5 face_mappings, and /v1/face-detection is free. The right plan is ONE mapped swap: the man in the light-blue shirt gets portrait-man.jpg, the blonde woman gets portrait-woman.jpg, and everyone else is left alone. I would map the man in the exchange with the woman (light-blue shirt, foreground) and leave the bearded man in navy unchanged.

Photo Speaks My Short Script

47

Make this photo of me talk in an 8-second square video. Say exactly: “Hi everyone! Thanks for stopping by. I can't wait to show you what's new.” Use a friendly female English voice, not a clone of mine. No captions.

broke at: Executor voice + agent-reasoning Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The chain is right (exact script with write, then a synthetic female voice, then talking-photo of her own picture), and the words and identity came out right. The length was handled by hope. The plan had "Target delivery length: 8 seconds" in write and "pace delivery to exactly 8 seconds" in the voice extra, which voice.js passes to gpt-4o-mini-tts as a style instruction that it ignores. It also set seconds: 8 on voice, talking-photo and crop, and no code reads any of those. So the voice came out at 5.06 s, Magic Hour's talking photo took the audio's length (end_seconds = the sound's length, 5.12 s), and the crop kept 5.13 s. The agent had what it needed to see this coming: the planner prompt says "A voice track's length sets the clip length that carries it", and the write line gives 2.5 words a second, so 14 words is about 5.5 s and 8 s needs about 2.5 s of pauses that no listed tool adds. The final crop was also wasted: the portrait and the talking clip are already 640x640. I would build the 8 s into the voice track itself: one sentence per line, an unhurried delivery with a pause after each, and the track padded to exactly 8.0 s.

evidence from the files
ffprobe: speech.mp3 is 5.06 s; talking-portrait.mp4 is 640x640, 5.12 s, with audio; talking-portrait-square.mp4 is 720x720, 5.13 s. The grader frames show the curly-haired woman with changing mouth shapes. voice.js never reads params.seconds and sends extra as the TTS 'instructions'. execute.js builds talking-photo with end_seconds = the sound's length. The grader's 'about 8 s' window is 6.4 to 9.6 s, so 5.1 s fails correctly.

Fix Make voice.js honour params.seconds. After synthesis, if the speech is shorter than the target, spread the gap as pauses between lines (sentences) plus a short lead-in and tail (adelay/apad) until it is exactly the target. If it is longer, apply atempo up to 1.15 and report anything still over. Add to the catalogue's voice line: "its length sets talking-photo's length; seconds pads it with pauses". This applies to every timed voice-over and talking head, including E28b's 10 s narration.

C17b

Write My Talking Sale Pitch

47

Make this photo of me say something about our sale. You write the line—keep it upbeat and don't invent discounts, dates or products. An 8-second square talking video, friendly male English voice, no captions.

broke at: Planner + harness Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent wrote the line itself, inside the write prompt ('Write exactly this ... Do not add any words'): 12 words. That skipped the one thing the write node exists to guarantee, a stated length. The planner rule says 8 s is about 20 words, and the catalogue says 2.5 words a second. The agent then asked the voice to 'pace delivery to exactly 8 seconds' in extra. The voice tool cannot do that: it passes extra as a tone instruction to the TTS and returns however long the speech runs (4.46 s here). Talking-photo takes its length from the sound, so the video came out 4.5 s. The agent never checked that 12 words cannot fill 8 s. It seems to have assumed the voice or talking-photo would stretch to params.seconds. The sale line itself was good: upbeat, no invented discount, date or product. I would let write compose about 20 words with the no-claims constraint and the length as a constraint. I would then let the voice length set the clip, as the planner rule says.

evidence from the files
The script file holds 12 words: 'Our sale is here! Take a look and see what catches your eye.' sale-voice.mp3 is 4.464 s, and sale-talking-portrait.mp4 is 640x640, 4.52 s, with 4.48 s of audio. Frames tiled at 2 fps show the same grey-haired man in the kitchen, mouth shapes changing, and no captions. The output is right in every respect except length. The judge's 4.5 s versus 8 s fail is correct. voice.js has no duration control: extra goes to the TTS as tone 'instructions'. execute.js sets the talking-photo length from the sound's duration (lenOf(sndIn)).

Fix Harness: when a voice node has params.seconds (or feeds a node with seconds), measure the speech. If it is more than 15% off the target, rerun the write node with 'rewrite to N words', where N = round(seconds x words-per-second measured from this take), then re-voice. When the agent composes them, the length goes in extra ('length: about 20 words'). Catalogue: add 'CANNOT: stretch or pace speech to a length; the words set the length' to voice, and 'its length is the sound's length' to talking-photo.

D18a

Bottle Turns Slowly in Place

42

Animate this bottle turning slowly in place on the table, just a gentle quarter turn. Keep the camera still. Make it 6 seconds, square, no sound.

broke at: Model + agent-reasoning Claude's fix would pass: unlikely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The structure of the agent's plan is the one I would choose: one image-to-video of the user's photo, 6 s, 1:1, sound dropped by the harness. The difference is the prompt. The agent wrote 'preserve the bottle's appearance', which only describes the side the model can SEE. A quarter turn forces minimax to invent the side it cannot see, and an unbranded black bottle invites a printed logo there. That is what happened: white garbled vertical lettering and a round badge rotated into view. The agent did not anticipate that rotation reveals unseen surfaces, and nothing in the catalogue warns about it. It also did not say the cap's carry loop is a rigid part, and the loop bent into an open hook mid-turn. I would state that the bottle is plain matte black on EVERY side with no print anywhere, that the cap and loop are one rigid moulded piece turning with the body, and that the camera is locked off on a tripod. That improves the odds, but the deformation and hallucination are minimax-at-480p behaviour that no prompt fully controls.

evidence from the files
product-bottle.jpg (640x640) shows a completely plain matte black bottle with a black cap and a closed carry loop seen face-on, on a wooden table by a window. bottle-quarter-turn.mp4 is 480x480, 6.58 s, video stream only (silent). A 1 fps strip shows the loop turning (so the rotation did happen), then from about 2 s a white vertical garbled word ('soap'l ele'-like) and a small round badge rotating onto the body. At about 2 s the loop becomes an open hook, and the bottle drifts slightly left. The background is broadly stable with small shifts. The judge's faults (invented branding, morphing loop, slight drift) match what is visible, so the grader is right. 144 credits (6 s at 24/s).

Fix Add a catalogue line to image-to-video: 'POORLY: turning a product: it paints a logo or text on the side it cannot see and bends thin parts (a loop, a handle, a strap); say the product is plain/unbranded on every side and its parts are rigid, or give an end frame'. Add a planner PROMPTS rule: for any rotation or orbit of a supplied product, describe the hidden side explicitly (same finish, no print) and name the rigid parts. A cheap harness guard: frame at 50% and 100% plus a check ('any text or logo on the product that is not in the source photo?'), retrying once with the negative strengthened when it flags.

Portrait With Subtle Natural Motion

46

Make this photo feel alive for 5 seconds: a natural blink and tiny breathing movement, nothing dramatic. Keep her face looking exactly like her throughout, no drifting or reshaping. Same square framing, still camera, no sound.

broke at: Model + agent-reasoning + harness Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent's tool choice was right (image-to-video of the supplied portrait, 5 s, 1:1, sound dropped) and its prompt asked for only a blink and breathing. Two things I would do differently: (1) give the portrait as BOTH start and end picture, the catalogue's own 'seamless loop' strength, so the model has to bring her face back to exactly where it started, which strongly damps the sideways drift it produced; (2) describe the only motions positively (she holds still, blinks once, one slow breath, locked-off tripod) instead of a list of forbidden motions ('no head movement, facial reshaping...'), which video models often read as cues. Its verification step could not work: check takes a picture, received the source and the clip, saw one image and flagged 'cannot verify', so nothing caught the sway.

evidence from the files
portrait-woman.jpg is a 640x640 head-and-shoulders photo (curly dark hair, grey knit sweater, park). portrait-animated.mp4 is 480x480, 5.17 s, 24 fps, no audio stream (silence correct). Block-matching the face region against frame 0 at 240 px scale: the face drifts left by 4 px at 1.0 s, 11 px at 2.0-2.25 s (about 4.6% of the frame width), comes back to 5-6 px and ends at 8 px, while the background patch stays at 0 shift: the camera is still but she sways sideways, which is exactly the judge's major fault. identity-check.json: 'Only one image is visible, so consistency ... cannot be verified.'

Fix 1) Planner rule / catalogue line for image-to-video: 'a photo that should just come alive (blink, breath, hair in the wind) -> the same picture as start AND end, motion described positively, no list of forbidden motions'. 2) Harness: let check take a clip (sample 4-6 frames plus the source) and allow one regeneration on a drift or sway verdict; today it saw one image and could only flag. 3) Longer term, a driven 'portrait-live' tool (keypoint-driven blink/breath on the still, LivePortrait-style) that keeps identity and position locked by construction.

Lake Clouds and Water Moving

42

Turn this lake photo into an 8-second silent video. Let the clouds drift slowly and little ripples move across the water. Keep the mountains and trees still, same wide framing and evening light. No camera movement.

broke at: Model + spec Claude's fix would pass: unlikely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The plan is close to mine: one image-to-video of lake.jpg, 8 s, generated audio dropped, no aspect forced, and a prompt that names what moves (clouds, ripples), what stays (mountains, trees), the locked camera and the evening light. minimax-h3 still turned the 8 s into a dusk time-lapse: the clouds re-form and turn grey, and by the last frame the alpenglow on the peaks and the coloured reflections are gone. The agent missed a constraint the catalogue offers ("a seamless loop: the same picture as start and end"): giving lake.jpg as both the start and end picture forces the last frame back to the photo's warm light and cloud positions, which caps how far the model can drift. I would also word the motion as real time ("not a time-lapse; the light does not change"). One judge fault is not the agent's: the attachment the spec calls 16:9 is 640x384 (5:3). The clip kept that shape (788x480), and "same wide framing" argues for keeping it.

evidence from the files
lake.jpg is 640x384 (5:3); the output is 788x480, 8.0 s, with no audio stream. Grader frame at 1 s: warm alpenglow on the peaks, pink clouds and coloured reflections, matching the photo. Frame at 7 s: peaks grey, clouds re-formed and grey, reflections gone. The mountains, shoreline and trees stay aligned. The judge is right about the time-lapse clouds and the fading light, and wrong that the clip should be 16:9.

Fix Add a planner rule or catalogue WELL line: "animate only part of a still and keep its light and framing → image-to-video with the same picture as start and end, motion worded as real-time". Also fix the spec: when the brief says "same framing", the expected aspect is the attachment's own ratio (lake.jpg is 5:3, not 16:9).

Dog Catches a Flying Frisbee

41

Make a realistic 5-second widescreen video of a golden retriever catching a red frisbee in a grassy park. One continuous shot with the camera staying still, no sound.

broke at: Grader + model-limit + agent-reasoning Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The plan matches mine: one text-to-video with no reference, 5 s at 16:9, and the invented sound dropped by code. The agent's prompt asked for the catch but did not stage it. It never said where the frisbee comes from, how long it flies or when the catch happens. So minimax spent 3.5 s on the dog running at the camera and squeezed the throw and catch into the last 1.2 s, with the disc dropping in from the top edge of the frame. The catch is real but brief. The judge's sparse frames (about 1.3 s apart) jumped from an empty mouth to a frisbee already held, so it marked the flight as missing. I would write the action beat by beat (thrown in from the left, a slow arc, the catch at mid-clip, trotting off with it) so the flight fills a second or more of the clip and any frame sampling catches it.

evidence from the files
golden_retriever_frisbee.mp4 is 858x480, 5.17 s, 24 fps, video stream only (no audio). Frames at 4 fps show the dog running at the camera with an empty mouth from 0 to 3.5 s. At 12 fps from 3.3 to 4.5 s, the red frisbee enters at the top edge (about 3.5 s), descends over about 5 frames to the dog's open mouth, briefly covers its face, and is held in the mouth from about 4.3 s to the end. The disc stays red and whole throughout, never disappearing. The tree trunk on the right holds its position, so the camera is static. Must-haves 2 and 3 are met, though the flight is short. The judge's 'no approaching frisbee is visible' comes from sparse sampling, and its audio 'cannot_tell' should have been a yes.

Fix Grader: sample the clip densely, or at least around motion peaks (for example 4 to 8 fps over the whole clip, or the frames with the largest optical-flow change), before judging an action that lasts under a second. Read the audio from the container: this file has no audio stream at all, so 'no audible sound' is a definite yes, not cannot_tell. Planner: add a prompt rule for actions in text-to-video and image-to-video: 'describe the action in order with its timing (enters from, travels, happens at about the middle, ends with), so the key moment is not squeezed into the last second'.

Hands Fold a Paper Sheet

58

Make an 8-second realistic widescreen video looking down at a person's hands folding a plain blue sheet of paper in half on a wooden table, then pressing the crease flat. Keep both hands and the whole sheet in view. One fixed shot, no sound.

broke at: Model + agent-reasoning Claude's fix would pass: unlikely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

There is no material to start from, so a single text-to-video shot is correct, at 8 s and 16:9 with sound dropped by code. Where we differ is the prompt. The agent packed the whole action into one clause ('fold the sheet in half, align the edges, then press the crease flat') with no timing, no fold direction and no limit on how many folds. minimax read that as 'some paper folding'. It collapsed the sheet into a narrow, multiply-creased strip in about 0.5 s (0.75–1.25 s), then filled the remaining 7 s with invented origami: diagonal flaps and an envelope shape by 7 s. I would pace the single action across the 8 seconds (fold over 0–4 s, press over 4–8 s), name the fold (bottom edge up to the top edge, one horizontal crease), and say what never happens (no second fold, no flaps, the sheet is never lifted or turned). The agent did not know that a video model compresses a one-line action into the first second and then improvises to fill the time. Even so, hands manipulating paper at 480p remain a hard case for minimax.

evidence from the files
paper_fold.mp4 is 858x480, 8.0 s, video only (silent). At 4 fps over the first 2.4 s: a flat landscape sheet at 0–0.5 s, then a lift and buckle into vertical creases, and by 1.25 s a narrow strip with several vertical folds. A 1 fps grid then shows the hands pressing (2–4 s), diagonal flaps appearing (4–6 s), and at 7 s the paper turned into a horizontal envelope or triangle shape. The hands are anatomically fine and both stay in frame, and the camera is fixed. The judge's major fault (extra folds, envelope-like result) and minor fault (pronounced vertical folds by 1 s) match the frames, so the grader is right.

Fix Add a planner PROMPTS rule for video: an action with an end state (fold, pour, stack, tie, write) is paced across the clip ('from 0 to 4 s …, from 4 to 8 s …'), says how many times it happens ('folded exactly once') and names what never happens. Otherwise the model finishes the action in the first second and invents more to fill the length. Add a catalogue line to text-to-video: 'POORLY: hands working an object (paper folds, knots, cards): it rushes the action and adds steps; pace it in the prompt'.

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent's plan matches mine in shape: an instrumental music bed and one assemble of the five photos in the attached order, 9:16, 10 s, no text. It asked assemble for 'smooth cross-dissolves' and 'fit photos without cropping' in extra, but the catalogue line for assemble mentions no transitions and the code ignores both: it concatenates with hard cuts and crops every photo to fill. The agent had no way to know its extra was dropped, and the tool reported success. The fail was then pinned on 'speech' in the soundtrack, which the evidence says is a transcription hallucination on instrumental music, not vocals. So the reel's real defect (hard cuts where the user asked for smooth transitions) is the harness's, and the grader failed it for the wrong reason.

evidence from the files
cafe-reel.mp4 is 720x1280, 10.0 s, with AAC audio. Frame-difference analysis gives four single-frame jumps (mean abs diff 70-95) at 2.03, 4.03, 6.03 and 8.03 s and no ramps: hard cuts, no dissolves. Frames at 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 s show storefront, latte, pastries, barista and interior in the attached order, each centre-cropped to fill 9:16 with a slow push-in (the barista's face half cut); all recognisable, no text. cafe-music.mp3 (10 s, peak -1.8 dB): its 0-4 kHz spectrogram shows only flat, steady instrument harmonics and a regular backbeat, with no gliding or vibrato harmonics and no syllable-rate formant bursts that singing or speech would leave. The transcriber returned '끄덕끄덕' here and 'Dieu, tu es grand' for a different music file in run real-1: random-language fragments, the usual hallucination on instrumental audio.

Fix 1) Harness (assemble.js): support transitions: join the parts with xfade (fade/dissolve, 0.4-0.6 s) and lengthen each part by the overlap so the total stays exact; default to dissolves for a photo-only reel and to cuts only when asked; list 'transitions: cut | dissolve' on assemble's catalogue line. 2) Harness: when a step's extra asks for something the tool does not do (dissolves, fit without cropping), report it instead of returning success silently. 3) Grader: do not treat a few transcribed words over a music bed as singing; run a vocal/speech detector or re-transcribe with a 'this may be instrumental music' prompt and require a confident, sustained transcript before calling it speech; also sample frames around the cuts so transitions can be judged.

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent recorded "Make it fun! You pick the vibe" as tone=fun and then planned only the mechanics: one assemble of the five photos in input order, 1.6 s each, with no music, no captions and no comic beat. When the user hands over the vibe, making it fun is the producer's job: an upbeat track, a joke timed to each picture, cuts on the beat. The rule it followed ("photos for a reel go straight into assemble, no image-to-video unless they ask for motion") is about not animating needlessly. It says nothing about dropping the music, and the reel template next to it includes music. Its extra "fit full photos within the vertical canvas with padding rather than cropping" is also something assemble does not do: assemble crops every picture to fill 9:16. So the 5:3 beach photo was cut to its middle third, clipping both friends' faces at the sides, and the 5:3 lake was blown up soft. The catalogue's "the user's photos used as they are" made the agent think otherwise. I would fit the two landscape photos first with crop fit: contain, lay a bouncy instrumental under the cut, and chain one comic caption per picture.

evidence from the files
photo-montage.mp4 is 720x1280, 8.0 s, with cuts at 1.6/3.2/4.8/6.4 s. Its audio track peaks at -91 dB (silent): no music. I extracted the frame at 4 s: the beach photo is centre-cropped, cutting off the man's left side and the woman's right side. The grader sampled 1/3/5/7 s and never saw it. The lake frame is visibly soft (a 384 px-tall picture stretched to 1280). There are no captions, music or transitions. The judge's 'not usable, no playful treatment' is fair.

Fix Add a planner rule: "fun / playful / you pick the vibe" on a photo reel means music plus a playful treatment (comic captions timed to each photo, or short image-to-video moves), never bare slides. Correct the catalogue's assemble line: it crops every picture to fill the aspect and gives stills a slow push-in, so the user's photos are not "used as they are". Keeping a whole landscape photo needs crop fit: contain first; alternatively make assemble honour "fit: contain" in extra. The same gap affects every 'make it fun/punchy' reel and every mixed-aspect photo reel.

Mixed Sizes Without Cropping

23

These photos are all different shapes. Make one 10-second vertical reel, in this order. Keep each whole photo visible—don't stretch or crop them. Use a soft blurred background to fill the gaps. No music or text.

broke at: Planner + harness + grader Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent sent the five raw photos straight into assemble and wrote the fitting rule into extra ('foreground: contain ... background: enlarged soft-blurred duplicate'). assemble reads none of that: it always scales to fill and centre-crops, then adds a push-in. The catalogue's CHOOSING line covers this exact case: keep ALL of a picture in a new size, 'blurred copy behind', means crop with extra 'fit: contain'. The agent skipped that per-photo step. It was probably misled by assemble's catalogue guarantee, 'the user's photos used as they are', which reads as 'never cropped', and by the habit of putting any requirement into extra as if the tool would honour free text. I would contain-fit each photo to 9:16 over a blurred copy first, then assemble the five fitted frames in order: 10 s, 9:16, no sound. The grader is wrong on one point. It failed 'silent' because the transcript reported a 'speech fragment' at -91 dB. That level is digital silence from the anullsrc track assemble adds. The cropping failures it reported are real.

evidence from the files
Inputs: storefront, barista and interior are 640x384, latte is 640x640, pastries is 384x640. The output cafe-reel.mp4 is 720x1280 and 10.0 s. Its AAC track measures -91.0 dB mean and max: true digital silence. Frames at 1 fps show every photo filling the frame edge to edge. The storefront has lost both sides, the latte is cut through the cup handle and saucer, and the barista frame shows only hands and a pitcher. No blurred background appears anywhere. assemble.js builds every picture as 'scale=...:force_original_aspect_ratio=increase,crop=...' plus a zoompan push-in and has no code path for contain. crop.js already implements 'fit: contain' with a boxblur background.

Fix (1) Catalogue: assemble's guarantee 'the user's photos used as they are' is false for any photo whose shape differs from the frame. Change it to 'pictures are cropped to fill the frame, with a slow push-in; to keep a whole photo, crop each with fit: contain first'. (2) assemble.js: honour 'fit: contain' or 'blur' in extra (reuse crop.js's contain filter), and when pictures are contain-fitted, turn off the 8% push-in, which still trims about 4% off each side of a full-width photo by the end of its shot. (3) Planner guard: if the sheet says 'keep the whole photo', 'don't crop' or 'blurred background' and a picture's aspect differs from the target, insert crop fit:contain before assemble. (4) Grader: anything below about -60 dB is silence; do not trust a transcript fragment from a silent track.

D21a

Quiet Lake Website Loop

82

Make a 6-second seamless loop for my website background: a calm mountain lake at dusk, with gentle ripples. Wide 16:9, camera staying still, no text or sound. Keep it subtle so I can put my own heading over it.

broke at: Executor clip length + model-limit Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent's plan is the catalogue's loop recipe and the one I would draw: a klein still, then image-to-video with that still as both start and end picture, 6 s, 16:9, sound dropped. Its prompts were sensible: fixed camera, only ripples, calm centre, no text. The failure happened after the model returned. minimax-h3 turns a 6 s request into 6.58 s (158 frames at 24 fps), and the harness conforms the aspect and audio but never the length, so a 6.6 s file shipped against an explicit '6-second'. Simply cutting to 6.0 s would also be wrong here: frame 144 (6.0 s) is further from frame 0 (SSIM 0.71) than the model's final frame is (0.86). The right finish is a loop-aware conform that crossfades the extra 0.58 s tail onto the head. That gives exactly 6.0 s with an identical first and last frame. Neither the agent nor the catalogue can express that: trim and assemble would both cut, and the seam would get worse.

evidence from the files
mountain_lake_loop.mp4 is 858x480, 24 fps, 158 frames = 6.583 s, video stream only (silent). Frames 0, 79 and 157 show a fixed, calm dusk lake with gently changing ripples and an open centre. Seam: frame 157 vs frame 0 has SSIM 0.86, while a normal step (frame 0 vs 1) is 0.94, and the final frames are nearly frozen (156 vs 157 SSIM 0.998). So the loop eases to a halt and then jumps slightly. A plain cut at 6.0 s would be worse (frame 144 vs 0 SSIM 0.71). The judge failed only the 6-second must-have (6.6 s) and could not judge the seam from stills, so the grader is right: the request said 6 s. Note the D18a judge called the same 6.6 s 'approximately six seconds', so the judge is inconsistent.

Fix Harness, in execute.js after every generated clip: conform the length to params.seconds. When the step's start and end picture are the same file (a loop), take d = duration - seconds and crossfade the clip's last d seconds into its first d seconds (an ffmpeg xfade of [d, L] with [0, d] at offset L-2d). The result is exactly params.seconds, and its last frame equals its first. Otherwise trim the tail, or retime with setpts when within ±10%. minimax-h3 overshoots systematically (4 s → 4.46, 5 → 5.17, 6 → 6.58, 7 → 7.29 across the b2 sessions), so this matters for every single-clip deliverable. Also add a catalogue line under image-to-video: 'a loop is closed and cut to the exact length by code'.

D22a

Make a Cat Then Animate

30

Make a square illustration of an orange cat wearing a blue scarf on a sunny windowsill, then animate that picture for 5 seconds: the cat blinks and gently swishes its tail. Send me both the picture and the silent video.

broke at: Model + agent-reasoning + grader Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent's chain is the right one (image, then image-to-video of that image, both kept) and the animation prompt is good: the cat blinks and swishes its tail, silent, square. The defect was born in the still: flux-2-klein drew the cat with two striped tails, and the 120-credit animation faithfully carried both. The agent's still prompt pushed 'with its tail clearly visible' without saying one tail or where it lies, and it animated without checking the 5-credit still first. I would name a single tail and its position, and gate the animation on a check of the still. The 'no standalone picture' finding is the grader's: the still exists, but deliverables() only counts sink nodes (plus a few code tools), so an intermediate the user asked for is invisible to it.

evidence from the files
cat_illustration.png (klein, 640x640) shows an orange tabby in a blue scarf on a sunny windowsill, with TWO striped tails: one curling forward on the sill left of the paws, a second hanging off the sill on the right. cat_animation.mp4 (480x480, 5.17 s, video stream only, so silent) carries both tails in every sampled frame (0, 1.25, 2.5, 3.75, 5 s); the cat's eyes are closed at ~1.25 s (blink) and the left tail swings, so the motion itself met the brief. The grader saw only the mp4 because the still is consumed by image-to-video and is not a sink.

Fix 1) Planner rule: when a generated still feeds an expensive animation, add a check of the still (anatomy, counts, text) before the clip, and state counts of body parts that will move (one tail). 2) Let a failed check trigger one regeneration of the still before the video step runs. 3) Plan schema and grader: let a step be marked deliver: true (the agent already said 'I'll deliver both'), and have deliverables() count marked intermediates, not only sinks; today a requested picture that feeds a video is never counted, so every 'picture and its animation' item fails 'too-few-outputs'.

Animate the Lighthouse Just Made

23

Make me a wide watercolor picture of a red-and-white striped lighthouse on a rocky coast at dusk. No writing. / Now turn that picture into a 6-second silent video, same wide shape. Have small waves roll against the rocks and the lighthouse beam slowly sweep across the water.

broke at: Executor sheet → planner hand-off + model-limit Claude's fix would pass: unlikely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

Turn 2 was planned sensibly: one image-to-video of the turn-1 picture, 6 s, locked camera, waves and a sweeping beam, sound dropped. But it animated a photograph, because the turn-1 prompt never said watercolour. The planner never saw the word: the sheet stored "watercolor" only as the quote of direction=stated, and the planner prompt prints `direction: stated (stated)`. Its turn-1 desired_state reads "One 16:9 image of a red-and-white striped lighthouse on a rocky coast at dusk". So the planner's STYLE rule ("lead with the style when one is asked") never had a style to lead with. A photographic start frame cannot become a watercolour clip. Separately, minimax lit the lamp and put a glow on the water but drew no sweeping beam. "The lighthouse beam slowly sweeping" needs a concrete visual (a pale shaft of light rotating from left to right), and even then a moving beam is a weak spot for this model. The harness also left the clip at 6.58 s, and the judge counted that against the 6 s ask.

evidence from the files
lighthouse_dusk.png (640x360) is a photograph: photoreal rocks and lighthouse, a smooth sky gradient, no washes or paper texture. The turn-1 prompt contains no style word. The sheet's direction quote is 'watercolor'. The animated clip is 858x480, 6.58 s, with no audio. In the grader frame at 2.5 s the lamp is lit with a glowing reflection, but there is no beam, and the waves break on the rocks. The judge is right on watercolour and the beam.

Fix Same path as A06d. Print stated fields' quotes to the planner (or fill `style` whenever direction=stated), and fix the STYLE guard regex in plan.js so it also matches plurals. Also trim generated clips to params.seconds in execute.js (minimax returned 6.58 s for 6). In the catalogue's image-to-video POORLY line, add: "moving light beams: describe them as a visible shaft that rotates; still unreliable".

Keep My Robot Recognizable

41

Draw a square cartoon of a little yellow robot with one big round eye and purple boots, holding a red watering can beside a pot of seedlings. / Animate this for 5 seconds, silent. Have it tip the can and water the seedlings. Keep this exact robot and drawing style—same single eye, yellow body and purple boots, not a redesigned character.

broke at: Planner + harness + grader Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The failure was set up in turn 1. The user asked to 'Draw a square cartoon of ...', and the agent's image prompt dropped the word 'cartoon' entirely ('A little yellow robot with one big round eye and purple boots, ... square composition'). The catalogue warns that illustration styles drift to photographic unless the style leads the prompt. flux-2-klein duly made a glossy 3D vinyl-toy render. The planner's STYLE guard, which prepends a named style such as 'cartoon', never fired. It reads only the sheet fields, and the sheet's subject quote left out 'cartoon': the style field is only filled when direction=needed. In turn 2 the agent was right to animate the session picture with image-to-video, and minimax kept that exact robot and its 3D look. So the clip fails the user's 'cartoon drawing' intent because the drawing never was one. A second, smaller miss: the turn-1 picture holds the can with its spout pointing away from the pot. In turn 2 the model had water come out of the handle side (the judge's 'double spout'). I would lead every prompt in the piece with the style. I would compose the turn-1 picture with the spout toward the pot, since watering is what a can beside seedlings is for. Then the turn-2 prompt would describe the can tipping forward so the water leaves the spout.

evidence from the files
Turn-1 yellow_robot_seedlings.png (640x640, flux-2-klein) is a glossy 3D vinyl-toy render with specular highlights and soft shadows, not a cartoon drawing. The can's spout and purple rose point to the right, away from the pot on the left. yellow_robot_watering.mp4 is 480x480, 5.17 s, video only (silent). Frames at 2 fps show the same toy robot: yellow body, one big eye, purple boots, the 3D look kept. Its head turns. The can tilts, the soil darkens or blues with water, and the stream leaves the handle side, not the spout. The output is faithful to the turn-1 picture, so the style failure was inherited from turn 1.

Fix Make the STYLE guard in plan.js read the user's raw messages for the whole session, not only the sheet's stated fields. 'Draw a square cartoon of ...' must make every image, image-edit and image-to-video prompt in the piece start with the style, follow-ups included. Fill the sheet's style field whenever a style word is said, not only when direction=needed. Grader: give the judge the turn-1 picture when a must-have compares against it, and read the audio from the container (this clip has no audio stream).

Mountain Morning Opening Title

52

Make a silent 6-second widescreen clip. Start with a dark green title card saying exactly “A quieter kind of morning” in cream lettering for 2 seconds, then cut to a slow moving shot of a misty mountain lake at sunrise. No other text.

broke at: Executor assemble Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent's decomposition was right: a qwen-lettered title card, a text-to-video lake shot, then assemble. It also stated the timing plainly in extra ('Hold title_card.png from 0 to 2 seconds; hard cut to sunrise_lake.mp4 from 2 to 6 seconds'). assemble.js reads no per-piece timing from extra. With seconds 6 and two pieces it gives each piece share = 6/2 = 3 s, so the picture got 3 s and the 4.46 s lake clip was cut to 3 s. The cut landed at 3.02 s. The catalogue promises assemble 'GUARANTEES the exact order, the exact length' but never says how the length is divided, so the agent had no reason to expect its timing to be dropped. I would get exact 2 s + 4 s from the current tools by making each piece its own length first: assemble the title alone for 2 s, trim the lake clip to 0–4 s, then assemble the two clips with seconds 0, which keeps clips at their own length. That only works if you know assemble's undocumented even split. The real defect is the harness silently ignoring stated timing.

evidence from the files
quieter_morning.mp4 is 1280x720, 6.02 s, with a silent audio track. Scene detection finds the only cut at 3.02 s. A 2 fps grid shows the title card in the first 6 frames (0–2.5 s), cream serif 'A quieter kind of morning' on flat dark green, correct and legible, then a misty sunrise lake with drifting mist. title_card.png is 626x352; sunrise_lake.mp4 is 4.46 s, video only. assemble.js computes share = T / vis.length, so each piece gets 3 s, and parses no timing from extra. The judge's only failure (title still on screen at 2.3 s, lake from 3.8 s) is accurate, so the grader is right.

Fix assemble.js: honour per-piece durations, via extra 'durations: 2, 4' or the 'from X to Y' wording planners already write, and let them override the even split. When the total is set and only some pieces have durations, give clips their own length and pictures the remainder rather than share = T/n. If a stated timing cannot be parsed, fail loudly instead of splitting evenly. Add to the catalogue line: 'per-piece seconds in extra (durations: 2, 4); otherwise pictures share what the clips leave'.

Gardener Interview Name Caption

39

Make a silent 7-second widescreen clip of a fictional woman standing in a community garden, smiling and turning slightly toward the camera. Put “Maya Chen” with “Community Gardener” underneath at the bottom left from second 1 through the end. White lettering on a dark backing, not over her face. No other text.

broke at: Planner + harness + model-limit Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent's chain (generate footage, then a code text-overlay with the exact words and timing) is right, and the overlay text itself came out exact. The decisive mistake was inside the footage prompt: to leave room it wrote 'clear space at bottom left for a lower third', and the video model took 'lower third' literally and painted a TV-style lower third (a circular 'ES' monogram and a teal banner of garbled words) at bottom left from about 0.5 s to the end; 'no text or signage' did not undo it. A generation prompt should describe only the scene and composition, never the graphics that will be added later. Second, the agent asked text-overlay for 'align: left', but the caption card is always centred horizontally, so the real caption landed bottom-centre on top of the fake banner; the catalogue does not say horizontal placement is impossible, so the agent could not know.

evidence from the files
garden_clip.mp4 (858x480, 7.29 s): the woman smiles and turns toward the camera in a garden with trellises; from ~0.5 s to the end the bottom-left 200x80 region holds a model-drawn lower third: a circular 'ES' monogram and a dark teal banner reading 'RagMirinsnlen / Vagon Trotents', fading to the monogram at the end. maya_garden_final.mp4: our card reads exactly 'Maya Chen' over 'Community Gardener', white on a translucent dark box, absent at 0.5 s and present from 1 s, but centred at the bottom (captionCard computes bx=(W-bw)/2), overlapping the fake banner. Both files have a video stream only (silent). The footage prompt contained 'clear space at bottom left for a lower third'.

Fix 1) Planner rule: a generation prompt describes the scene only; never name the overlay ('lower third', 'title', 'caption', 'space for text') in it, because video and image models draw what they are told about. Say 'leave the lower left uncluttered' in plain composition terms instead. 2) Harness: text-overlay/captionCard accepts align: left|center|right (left = 5% margin, left-aligned lines) and the catalogue line says so; today 'align: left' is silently ignored and every card is centred. 3) Run a check for unwanted text on generated footage (frame + check) before overlaying.

Coffee Clip Exact URL Ending

32

Make a silent 8-second vertical coffee clip: a close-up of coffee being poured into a ceramic cup for 5 seconds, then a plain black end card for the last 3 seconds. Center this exact URL in white: https://example.com/Go?ref=June — keep the capitals and punctuation exactly as typed, all on one line. Nothing else written anywhere.

broke at: Tool pick + harness + model-limit + grader Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent treated the URL as words laid over the clip and built the end card itself, from a flux-2-klein "completely uniform solid black frame" plus a code overlay. Both halves broke. Flux read "black frame" as a picture frame and drew a white panel inside a black border. The overlay sized the 31-character URL at 1/12 of 720 px (60 px), which is wider than the frame, and a URL has no spaces, so the 80% word-wrap could not break it and both ends were cut off. The plan has no size param, so "fit within frame with safe margins" did nothing. assemble also ignored "coffee 5 s, card 3 s" and split 8 s equally (the cut is at 4.02 s), so the card sat blank from 4 to 5 s. The catalogue's own CHOOSING rule routes "a title or end card" to one image node with lettering: true. qwen draws the plain black card and the exact URL together, and code reads the URL back and fixes a misspelling once. That is the tool I would use, followed by assemble with seconds 0, so the 5 s pour keeps its length and the card gets 2.5 s.

evidence from the files
black_end_card.png (360x640) is a white rectangle inside a black border: flux read 'frame' literally. In the grader frame at 7 s there is a white panel, a grey 55% band, and the URL cut at both edges ('ps://example.com/Go?ref=J'). Scene detection on silent_sequence.mp4 puts the cut at 4.02 s, not 5 s. coffee_final.mp4's audio peaks at -91 dB (silent), yet the judge was told speech was heard. The two major faults are real.

Fix (1) text-overlay: shrink the font until the longest unbreakable line fits 90% of the frame width, and accept "size:" in extra (the catalogue already says "unless the size is set", but the plan cannot set it). (2) assemble: honour per-piece durations given in extra ("coffee_pour.mp4: 5 s; card: 3 s") instead of an equal split. (3) Add a catalogue line: "plain colour card with exact words (end card, URL card) → image with lettering: true". (4) Grader: never report "speech heard" on a track whose peak is below -60 dB.

Spanish Subtitles For This Clip

29

Add Spanish subtitles to this English clip, please. Leave her voice in English and keep the whole video as it is.

broke at: Catalogue + agent-reasoning + harness Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

Translated subtitles need the clip's words and their timing as TEXT. Nothing in the catalogue produces that. captions 'makes a clip' (English burned into pixels, ignores the language), write cannot hear audio, and text-overlay draws one text with one from/to. The agent papered over the gap by inventing capabilities the catalogue never offered: captions 'export timed subtitles as SRT', write 'preserve SRT timestamps', text-overlay 'use subtitle-file timings throughout'. The harness then failed silently at each step. The non-existent input 'english-subtitles.srt' was resolved to the burned-in english-subtitles.mp4 through the file-variant lookup. write, which only reads .txt/.md/.json context, ran with no words and returned 'Envía los subtítulos en inglés que quieres traducir.' ('Send the English subtitles you want to translate'). text-overlay burned that sentence over all 10 s. An expert would see that the catalogue cannot get a transcript out of the clip. The options are a transcription step, or telling the user that only English captions are possible today. The agent should not have planned a chain whose middle link carries no data.

evidence from the files
spanish-subtitles.txt holds exactly 'Envía los subtítulos en inglés que quieres traducir.' The job log shows write ran with inputs ['english-subtitles.srt'], a file that never existed, and text-overlay used that sentence as its text. The captions output english-subtitles.mp4 (858x480, 10.1 s, 53 cr) has correct burned English cues: 'Hi everyone.' at about 1-2 s, 'Today I want to show you three easy' at about 2-6 s, and 'ways to make your mornings less stressful.' at about 6-10 s. That proves the speech is recoverable, but only as pixels. The final talk-one-spanish-subtitles.mp4 keeps the original footage and audio (10.13 s) with the one unrelated Spanish sentence throughout. The judge's verdicts match.

Fix (1) Add a 'transcribe' code tool: clip to timed .srt via OpenAI speech-to-text, 0 Magic Hour credits. (2) Let write read .srt context. (3) Let text-overlay take a .srt input and burn each cue at its time, reusing captionCard and burnCaptions from lib/captions.js. With these three, the plan above is 'likely'; with today's catalogue the honest outcome is 'no'. (4) Harness: a declared input that does not exist must fail the step, not resolve to another extension's file (english-subtitles.srt became english-subtitles.mp4). A write node given an input it cannot read must fail. Flag a write output that is a request for input instead of the asked text before anything consumes it. (5) Catalogue: captions 'CANNOT: give back the words as text; translate'. text-overlay: 'one text, one time range per node'.

Silent Clip Subtitle Check

0

Can you subtitle this clip? If there's no speech in the audio, just tell me.

broke at: Catalogue + agent-reasoning + harness Claude's fix would pass: yes

Nothing made

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The question is purely factual: does this file contain speech? The system has no way to listen. 'check' is a vision call that 'takes picture', so the agent wired a clip into a picture-only tool. It failed with 'check needs a picture', execution stopped, and the user's last messages were two copies of 'check failed: check needs a picture' with no answer. The agent also asked an unneeded question ('Which language?'). The default is the clip's own language, the user had framed the job as conditional, and the expected behaviour was never to ask. Its plan was conditional ('captions … run only if speech-check.json confirms audible speech'), but the harness has no conditionals. Had the check passed, captions would have run and spent credits regardless. I would answer without any generative step. talk-one-silent.mp4 has no audio stream at all (ffprobe: one h264 video stream, 10.1 s), so the honest reply is that there is nothing to subtitle. The agent could not know this, because the planner only ever sees the file NAME.

evidence from the files
materials/talk-one-silent.mp4: ffprobe shows a single h264 video stream (858x480), duration 10.125 s, and NO audio stream; volumedetect reports 'Output file does not contain any stream'. session.json messages: the user's request, then the question 'Which language?', the answer 'English if there is audible speech', the plan sentence, and then 'check failed: check needs a picture' twice. Nothing was made (assets/tree-2 is empty). The judge correctly failed 'clearly states that the clip has no audible speech' and the unneeded question.

Fix Smallest change: probe every material before planning and put the facts in the MATERIALS line, e.g. 'talk-one-silent.mp4 (clip, 858x480, 10.1 s, audio: none)' (ffprobe streams + volumedetect; 'audio: silent' when the peak is below about -60 dB). Add a planner rule: a question the facts answer (is there sound or speech, how long, what size) is answered in say with no steps. For speech, as opposed to just sound, add a 'probe' code tool (inspect group): clip or sound → {has_audio, peak_db, speech: yes/no, first words} using a speech-to-text model at 0 Magic Hour credits. Also make 'check' accept a clip, by sampling frames, instead of throwing, and when a step fails, send the user a plain answer rather than the raw error. The intake should not ask for a caption language when the default is the clip's own language.

Make Those Captions TikTok Bold

0

Add English subtitles to this clip. Keep her original voice. / Make them big and bold for TikTok. Make the video vertical too, but keep her face in view.

broke at: Planner + harness + wrong-tool Claude's fix would pass: likely

Nothing made

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

Turn 1 (captions on the clip) was right. In turn 2 the agent treated the turn-1 subtitles as editable objects: it cropped the already-captioned clip to 9:16, which cut the burned-in subtitle lines at both sides ('ant to show you t', 'your mornings l'), and then asked a generative video-edit to 'restyle the existing subtitles'. Burned-in captions are pixels; they cannot be restyled, only redone. The right move is to go back to the clean source: crop the original talk-one.mp4 to vertical around her centred face, then caption that vertical clip with a big, bold style placed above TikTok's bottom controls. Its tool, video-edit, was offered by the catalogue at the time but had no endpoint, so nothing was made (the WIRED/OFFERED filter added since then removes it). Even the right plan meets a harness limit: captions always sends the 'minimalist' template, so 'big and bold' cannot be requested today.

evidence from the files
talk-one.mp4 is 858x480, 10.1 s with speech; the speaker is centred. Turn 1's talk-one-subtitled.mp4 carries small white 'minimalist' subtitles near the bottom ('Today I want to show you three easy', 'ways to make your mornings less stressful.'). Turn 2's talk-one-vertical.mp4 is 720x1280 and its burned-in subtitles are cut at both sides ('ant to show you t', 'your mornings l'). Step 2 (video-edit) has no endpoint and returned only talk-one-tiktok-subtitled.svg, a placeholder, so nothing was delivered (score 0). execute.js sends captions with style: { template: 'minimalist' } whatever the plan asks.

Fix 1) Keep the OFFERED filter (only wired tools reach the planner); it would have stopped video-edit. 2) Planner rule: captions are burned in; to restyle, resize or reframe a captioned clip, start again from the uncaptioned source (crop or trim first, caption last), never crop a captioned clip. 3) Harness: the captions call hard-codes style {template: 'minimalist'}; map the plan's style words to the subtitle API's style (a bold/TikTok-type template, or custom font size, weight, stroke and vertical position) and update captions' catalogue line from 'POORLY: big and bold is not honoured' to the supported options.

Turn this into a 9:16 vertical clip. Show the man when he asks his question, then the woman when she answers, with each centred while talking. Keep all 10 seconds and the original audio. No captions.

broke at: Planner + missing-tool + harness Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent planned one crop with "anchor: active speaker; centre the man throughout his question, then centre the woman throughout her answer". That assumes a speaker-tracking reframe the catalogue never offers: crop takes one anchor (left/right/top/bottom/center) for the whole clip. crop.js did not recognise "active" and silently used centre, which frames the dark-shirted bystander in the middle for all 10 s. The questioner is cut at the left edge and the woman is off frame. With the tools listed, the correct plan is to split at the turn: trim the clip at the speaker change, crop each part on its own speaker, then assemble the parts with seconds 0. Assemble keeps clip sound, and seconds 10 would cap each part at 5 s and cut the question. Two gaps made this harder. The agent cannot hear the clip, so it could not know the turn falls at about 7.9 s: there is no transcribe or timing tool. And neither left nor right puts these faces in the middle; the crop tool's undocumented "box: x,y,w,h" does. I measured the turn and the face positions myself.

evidence from the files
talk-two.mp4 is 858x480, 10.1 s. silencedetect finds speech at 6.42–7.67 s and 8.19–10.1 s, and nothing but low ambience before 6.4 s. In my frame at 7 s the light-shirted man on the left (face x≈180–340) is talking. The woman is on the right (face x≈595–730), and the dark-shirted man stands in the middle. The output is 720x1280, 10.13 s: my frames at 7 s and 9.2 s show the centre crop on the middle man, the questioner cut at the left edge and only a sliver of the woman's hair. The judge is right.

Fix (1) Add a transcribe tool: clip to text with segment times (gpt-4o-transcribe, 0 Magic Hour credits), so "when he asks / when she answers" becomes trim points. (2) Add to the catalogue for crop: "one static anchor per clip; to follow speakers: trim at each turn, crop each part, assemble with seconds 0"; expose a position ("box: x,y,w,h" or "anchor: 30%"). (3) Make crop fail on an unknown anchor instead of silently centring. (4) Make assemble's seconds a total, not a per-piece cap, so seconds 10 cannot truncate a 7.9 s part.
