Vertical Speaker Cut With Captions

61

Make this 9:16 with her centred and add readable English captions matching what she says. Keep the whole 10 seconds and her original voice. Put the captions below her face.

broke at: Executor captions + model-limit Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The plan is the one I would make. A code crop to 9:16 with her centred (she is already central, so anchor centre works), then captions on the cropped clip so the subtitles are laid out for the final frame, with the original audio kept. The agent even asked in extra for captions 'below her face'. The miss is in our captions call. execute.js always sends style {template: 'minimalist'}: white text with only a faint shadow. Over her white sweater, 'show you three easy' and 'mornings less stressful' wash out. The API's style.custom_config takes stroke_color/stroke_width, font_style bold and vertical_position, but the harness never passes any of them. It also ignores whatever the planner writes in extra. The catalogue then blames the tool ('styling: big and bold is not honoured'). The agent could not have fixed the contrast with catalogue tools. text-overlay's dark band would need the transcript, which nothing in the catalogue provides. The 'Hi everyone.' versus 'Hi everyone!' punctuation is the transcriber's choice and minor.

evidence from the files
talk-centred.mp4 is 720x1280 at 10.13 s, and the captioned output is 576x1024 at 10.0 s with audio. Frames at 1 fps show her centred with her whole face visible. Captions run in timed chunks: 'Hi everyone.' at about 1-2 s, 'Today I want to / show you three easy' at about 2-5 s, 'ways to make your / mornings less stressful.' at about 6-10 s, all words in order. They are thin white sans-serif with a faint shadow, sitting on her white sweater and hair. At 4 s, 'show you three easy' has very low contrast against the sweater. The judge's single contrast failure is fair. execute.js hard-codes style: { template: 'minimalist' }, and the API sheet (section 6.4) documents stroke_color, stroke_width and vertical_position in custom_config.

Fix In execute.js, send captions a style.custom_config, not a bare template: text_color #FFFFFF, stroke_color #000000, stroke_width about 3-4 px at 480p, font_style bold. Map vertical_position from the planner's extra ('position: top|center|bottom'), defaulting to bottom. Alternatively, pick a template with a stroke or box (test cinematic and highlight once). Then update the catalogue's captions lines to state what is actually controllable: position, an outlined high-contrast style, and no language choice.

Cut the boring parts out of this. Just a quick 8-second version.

broke at: Catalogue + wrong-tool + harness Claude's fix would pass: likely

Nothing made

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent picked 'video-edit' (Magic Hour's generative ai-video-editor). It was not wired, so the harness wrote a placeholder SVG and reported the step 'done'. Even if wired, it was the wrong tool: a generative editor re-renders footage, and the must-haves demand only source footage with no speed change and the original audio in sync. A cut is a code job, 'trim' (exact range, nothing regenerated), and the catalogue had it. But trim needs a 'from' and 'to', and choosing the 8 interesting seconds needs to SEE the clip. The planner only gets the filename, and no catalogue tool turns a clip into a shot list with timestamps, so the agent had nothing to choose a range from. It probably reached for video-edit because it is the only tool that sounds like it decides what to cut. Looking at the clip: 0–3 s jets cruising, 3–11 s cockpit lines ('Hook, you with me?' / 'Right here, Vega.'), 11.4–16.6 s a static ship with a caption card and a targeting display, 16.6–25.7 s missile launch, hits and the ship exploding, 25.7–29 s jets leaving, then an end card. The best 8 s is the continuous action from the 16.57 s scene cut to 24.57 s.

evidence from the files
assets/jet-8s.svg is a 906-byte placeholder; no video was made. jet-30s.mp4 is 1280x720, 30 fps, 30.0 s, with AAC audio, and the only silence is the last 1.06 s. Scene cuts at 3.0, 6.2, 9.3, 11.4, 14.5, 16.57, 25.7 and 28.8 s. The 1 fps grid shows the cockpit dialogue (with burned-in lines 'Hook, you with me?', 'Right here, Vega.') from 3 to 11 s, a static ship with 'MERIDIAN RANGE. HARROW: DECOMMISSIONED TARGET.' from 11.4 to 14.5 s, a targeting display from 14.5 to 16.6 s, missiles, hits and fireballs from 16.6 to 25.7 s, jets departing, and a black end card 'F-35C. TOGETHER, ON TARGET.' The judge's failure (nothing made) is correct.

Fix (1) Add a code 'analyse-clip' inspector (scene cuts via ffmpeg, one described frame per shot, plus a transcript) whose output is a shot list the planner reads. Or run it automatically on every supplied clip and put a short shot list in the MATERIALS line. (2) Planner rule: shortening or 'cutting the boring parts' of the user's footage is trim (one range) or trim + assemble (several ranges), never a generative video editor. (3) The b2 run offered the unwired video-edit, and the executor marks a placeholder 'done'. OFFERED now filters unwired tools, but a placeholder should also make the node 'failed: not wired' so the user hears it.

Add My Supplied Voiceover

42

Add a warm, clear English voice-over to this silent clip, saying exactly: “Make mornings easier: prepare your clothes, pack your bag, and plan breakfast the night before. Start tomorrow with less stress.” Keep the video unchanged. No music or captions.

broke at: Executor voice Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent's plan is right: the exact supplied words to a voice, laid over the user's silent clip with assemble, no music, no captions, the clip's own length kept. (The write step is redundant, since voice could take the words directly, but harmless: narration.txt holds the exact script.) The words were lost inside our voice tool: it reads any line that starts 'Capitalised words: ...' as a 'Name: line' dialogue label, so 'Make mornings easier:' became a speaker name and was never spoken. Nothing in the catalogue warns about that, and the agent could not have known. Knowing it, I would keep the exact words but replace the colon after 'easier' with a dash in the voice input, which reads the same aloud.

evidence from the files
narration.txt reads exactly 'Make mornings easier: prepare your clothes, pack your bag, and plan breakfast the night before. Start tomorrow with less stress.' voice.js splits lines with /^([A-Z][\w .'-]{0,24}):\s+(.+)/, which matches 'Make mornings easier' as a speaker name, so only the rest was sent to text-to-speech: narration.mp3 is 6.86 s, short for 21 words, consistent with 17 spoken, and the judge's transcript starts at 'Prepare your clothes'. talk-one-voiced.mp4 is 1280x720, 10.1 s, the kitchen-table footage (upscaled from 858x480) with the narration; no music, no text.

Fix Harness (tools/voice.js): treat 'Label: text' as a speaker only when the plan marks the script as a dialogue (extra 'dialogue' or a write node made for two voices), or when at least two different labels each start a line and the label is a short name (one or two words, no verb); otherwise speak the whole line. Also have the voice step read its output back (transcribe and compare with the input words, as lettering is read back) and redo once on a missing word. Generalises: every script with a colon in its first sentence ('Pro tip: ...', 'Remember: ...') is clipped today.

Write Narration From The Clip

41

Watch this and write a short English voice-over explaining what's happening. Replace the original conversation with your narration, friendly and matter-of-fact. Keep all 10 seconds of footage unchanged, with no music or captions. You pick the wording and voice.

broke at: Catalogue + harness + agent-reasoning Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent "watched" the clip the only way its catalogue allows: three frames and three vision checks, then a script from what they show ("Two men and a woman smile toward the camera... then turn toward one another"). In a 10 s clip of two coworkers talking, what is happening is what they say (a schedule change; Mondays now start at nine), and frames cannot reveal it. No tool in the catalogue hears a clip. The only stand-in is a detour (captions, about 48 cr, then frame, then check to read the burned subtitles), and the agent did not think of it. It also never noticed that its narration said nothing about the conversation it was replacing. The second failure is in the harness. The agent asked assemble to "remove all original audio", but assemble always keeps a clip's own sound, and because the clip has speech it lays the added voice at 0.25 as if it were music. The original dialogue is still there at full level, louder than the narration. The judge marked that must-have cannot_tell; it is actually a miss.

evidence from the files
narration.txt reads 'Two men and a woman smile toward the camera in a bright office, then turn toward one another as one man looks on.', built from three frame descriptions with no audio consulted. Half-second RMS: the narration alone is -17 to -28 dB. In the output it is -32 to -40 dB during 0–6 s (×0.25), while the original dialogue at 6–10 s stays at -20 to -29 dB, identical to the source. The conversation was not removed and is louder than the narration. The judge's content verdict is right.

Fix (1) Add a transcribe tool: clip or sound to .txt with segment times (gpt-4o-transcribe, as the grader already uses), with the catalogue line "WELL: what people in a clip say, with times: a voice-over that explains a conversation, a recut by speaker". Add a planner rule: "explain what's happening / what they say" on a clip with speech means transcribe, then write. (2) Change assemble: accept "clip sound: drop|duck", and treat a voice input as speech on top, not as music under the clip's speech. The tool line already promises "music under speech, not over it". Both changes also serve E25b's speaker timing and any dub or voice-over request.

Fit Narration To Seven Seconds

18

Replace all the sound with a calm English narrator saying: “Above the clouds, every second counts. Stay focused, trust your training, and bring everyone safely home.” Fit it to this 7-second clip: start in the first half-second and finish “home” in the last half-second. Natural pace, no chopped words. Don't trim, loop, or slow the video; no captions.

broke at: Executor assemble + missing-tool + grader + spec Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent's chain is the catalogue's own recipe for narration (voice, then assemble), with the exact words verbatim and the clip untouched. That is my plan too. Its 'Remove all original audio' instruction went into assemble's extra, which assemble never reads. No catalogue tool can drop a clip's own sound: every video code tool maps 0:a. assemble always mixes the clip's audio in. Worse, it treats any added sound as music: because the clip has audio ('speech'), it puts the narration at volume 0.25 (about -12 dB) under the radio calls, then fades out the last second. So the transcriber heard only 'Rook, you with me?', and 'safely home' was faded away. The voice itself was fine: speech runs from 0 to 6.83 s, followed by 1.36 s of trailing silence, which already meets the 0-0.5 s start and 6.5-7.0 s end windows. The agent's 'target duration 6.8 seconds' was ignored but did not matter here. The only reasoning gap: it trusted free-text extra to change a tool's audio behaviour. The catalogue gave no 'replace sound' option, and an expert would have flagged that before running.

evidence from the files
narration.mp3 is 8.21 s long, with speech from 0 to 6.83 s and silence after. The source radio-lines.mp4 is 1280x720, 7.0 s, with radio dialogue at -19.5 dB mean. The output radio-lines-narrated.mp4 is 7.0 s at -19.4 dB mean, almost unchanged from the source, so the narration was mixed in at about a quarter level. assemble.js sets level 0.25 when any clip has audio, amixes [0:a] with it, and applies afade from L-1. The burned-in subtitles 'Rook, you with me?' and 'Right here, Vega.' are already in the source frames. The judge's 'dialogue captions despite no-captions' is wrong: no captions were added. Its narration verdicts are right.

Fix Changes to assemble.js: (1) Support extra 'sound: replace' (or 'clip sound: off'): build the clip pieces with -an or anullsrc so the clip's own audio is dropped. Have the planner set it whenever the sheet says 'replace the sound' or 'remove the original audio'. (2) Do not duck a VOICE input: duck only music (tell the two apart by the producing tool, voice or music). A narration over a clip goes at full level, and the clip's own sound, when kept, goes under it. (3) Fade only music. Trim a voice track's trailing silence instead of fading the last second, so a final word is never faded out. The voice tool should also trim leading and trailing silence and report its speech length against params.seconds. Catalogue: assemble 'extra sound: replace drops the clips' own sound'. Grader: text burned into the user's source footage is not 'added' text.

Append a Clean End Card

37

Keep this whole 7-second clip, then add a 2-second black end card with white text: 'Ready for takeoff?' and '@flightschool' underneath. Center both lines. Keep the original sound, but make the end card silent.

broke at: Executor assemble Claude's fix would pass: yes

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent's tree was right: a qwen-lettered black end card, then assemble with the user's clip first. Its extra said exactly what was wanted: 'retain all 7 seconds unchanged with original audio; hold end-card.png for 2 seconds'. assemble.js ignores per-piece timing. With seconds 9 and two pieces it sets share = 4.5, gives the clip min(7, 4.5) = 4.5 s and the picture 4.5 s, and so silently cut a third of the user's footage, which the catalogue says assemble keeps 'as they are'. This is the same defect as D23a. I would get 7 + 2 from today's tools by making the card a 2-second clip first (assemble on the card alone, seconds 2), then joining the two clips with seconds 0, which keeps each clip at its own length. The agent had no way to know the even split existed, because the catalogue only promises 'the exact length'.

evidence from the files
radio-lines.mp4 is 1280x720, 7.0 s, with audio. The output radio-lines-with-end-card.mp4 is 9.02 s, with scene changes at 3.36 s (cockpit 2) and 4.52 s (end card). silencedetect finds silence from 4.51 s to the end. A 1 fps strip shows cockpit footage for 0–4 s and the end card from 5 s on, reading 'Ready for takeoff?' / '@flightschool' in white on black, centred and correct. end-card.png is 640x352. So the clip lost its last 2.5 s and the card ran 4.5 s, exactly the share = 9/2 split in assemble.js. The grader is right.

Fix Same as D23a: assemble.js must honour per-piece durations (extra 'durations: 7, 2', or 'hold X for N seconds'). It must never shorten a supplied clip to make an even share unless the user asked to cut it. When a total is set, clips keep their full length and pictures get what remains (here 9 - 7 = 2 s). If the total cannot be met without cutting the user's clip, the node should fail or flag rather than cut.

Subtle Handle Watermark Throughout

32

Add @flightschool as a subtle watermark at the bottom right for this whole clip. Small white text, slightly see-through, with a faint shadow so it's still readable. Keep it away from the edges and leave everything else alone.

broke at: Executor text-overlay + missing-tool Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent's plan is what I would want: one code text-overlay on the user's clip with the exact handle, and it spelled out everything in extra (at: bottom; align: right; small; opacity 70%; faint shadow; edge padding 3%). The tool silently ignored all of it but 'at: bottom': text-overlay only reads text and at, always centres the card horizontally, sizes the font to a twelfth of the short side (about 60 px on 720p), and always draws a 55% black box with no shadow. So a 'subtle bottom-right watermark' came out as a big bottom-centre label that also sits on top of the clip's own burned-in subtitles ('Right here, Vega.'). The catalogue line hints at the band ('one plain font on a band') but says 'GUARANTEES placement' and 'grows large unless the size is set', while no size can be set. With today's tools the only alternative is image (lettering) of the handle on plain black, filter look: transparent, then place at bottom-right: right corner and size, but no translucency. The real answer is a watermark mode in text-overlay.

evidence from the files
radio-lines.mp4 is 1280x720, 7.0 s with audio, and already carries its own small subtitles at bottom centre ('Right here, Vega.'). radio-lines-watermarked.mp4 (1280x720, 7.0 s, audio kept) shows '@flightschool' exact, white, about 60 px tall, centred at the bottom on a dark translucent box, fixed for the whole clip and overlapping the clip's own subtitle line. text-overlay.js uses only params.text and params.at; captionCard centres the box (bx=(W-bw)/2) and fills it at 55% black; no opacity, shadow, size or alignment option exists.

Fix Harness (text-overlay.js + captionCard): read align (left|center|right), size (px or % of height), opacity, shadow and box (none|band) from extra, with margin; add a 'watermark' preset (small, right-aligned, about 70% white, soft shadow, no box, 4% inset). Update the catalogue line: text-overlay WELL 'a small text watermark or handle in a corner (extra: align, size, opacity, shadow, box: none)', and drop 'GUARANTEES placement' until placement options exist. Have the tool report extras it cannot honour instead of returning success.

Upbeat Reel Music Default

91

Can you make me some music? Something upbeat for a reel.

broke at: Bench test + grader Claude's fix would pass: yes

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

There is nothing to fault. "Some music, something upbeat for a reel" came with no length, so the agent picked 15 s (the music model's minimum and a standard reel length), asked for no vocals, and delivered one standalone file. The bench spec says seconds: 10, but the user's own answer sheet says "Length: your call", so the deterministic 'about 10 s' check failed a length the user left open. Every must-have the judge could assess was met or unassessable from a transcript. I would make the same call.

evidence from the files
upbeat_reel_music.mp3 is 15.0 s. Half-second RMS is -13 to -16 dB from 0.0 s, so there is no silent lead-in. It stays steady to 13.5 s, then fades naturally to -56 dB with no abrupt cut. The spectrogram shows dense, regular percussion (about four hits a second) and steady instrumental harmonics, with no vocal pitch contours. The only failed check is 'about 10 s = 15'.

Fix Fix the spec: set seconds to null (or a range such as 10–30) when the answer sheet says the length is the agent's call, and have the grader skip the length check then. Any open-length item has the same problem.

Exactly Fifteen Seconds of Music

41

I need a music bed that's exactly 15 seconds, no vocals. Style is up to you.

broke at: Executor transcriber + model-limit + grader Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The plan is the obvious one and matches mine: one music node, 15 s, an instrumental prompt (the harness also appends 'no vocals, no singing, no speech'). The judge failed it on 'audible speech', a single Khmer word ('អ្នកភូមិ។'). That is the classic speech-to-text hallucination on instrumental music. The spectrogram shows only steady pad harmonics and percussion transients, with no gliding formant contours. The real defect is one nobody flagged. The track's music stops abruptly at about 12.9 s, and the last 2.1 s sit at -50 to -60 dB (digital silence from 14.17 s). The model composed a shorter piece inside the 15 s it was asked for, so the bed does not fill its length. The agent could not have prevented it with catalogue tools: no code tool cuts a sound (trim takes only clips, and assemble needs two sounds). The harness asks the model for exactly the target length whenever it is 15 s or more, and cuts only when the target is under 15 s. I would write the prompt to discourage an ending ('plays right through, no ending, no fade, no silence'). The robust fix is in code: overshoot and cut.

evidence from the files
ambient_bed.mp3 is actually PCM WAV, 48 kHz stereo, exactly 15.000 s, mean -16 dB. RMS per 0.5 s is -9.6 to -30 dB through 13.0 s, then -49.6, -52.6, -54.2 and -60.1 dB for the last 2 s. silencedetect at -45 dB finds 14.17-15.0 s. The 150-3500 Hz linear spectrogram shows constant-pitch pad lines at about 820 Hz, 1.0 kHz and 2.5 kHz with regular percussive transients, and no vocal harmonics or pitch glides. The music cuts off sharply at about 12.86 s. The judge's only failing verdict (speech) is a transcription artefact, while the dead tail it marked cannot_tell is the real problem.

Fix Harness, music node in execute.js: always generate more than asked (sec = max(15, want + 5)) and cut to exactly want seconds with a short 0.3-0.5 s fade. Today it cuts only when want < 15. Trim trailing near-silence (below -45 dB) before measuring, and if music under -45 dB starts before want, generate again. Grader: do not treat a one-word transcript in an unrelated language on music as speech; require a sustained run of words, or confirm with a vocal-presence check. Also check the RMS envelope for a silent tail (here 13.0-15.0 s), which is what must-have 3 asks.

Calm Voice Reading Supplied Script

76

Make an audio-only voice-over, about 10 seconds, in a calm, reassuring voice. Read exactly: “Take a slow breath. Let your shoulders relax. There is nothing you need to rush right now.” No music or other sounds.

broke at: Executor voice + model-limit Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent chose the right tool and gave the exact words with the right intent: voice, calm, 'pace and pauses to fit 10 seconds', seconds 10. voice.js ignores params.seconds. It passes extra to gpt-4o-mini-tts as a style instruction and ships whatever length comes back, here 7.8 s: three phrases totalling about 5 s of speech, 0.9 s and 0.74 s pauses, and a 0.5 s lead and 0.6 s tail. The words are fixed (17 words; a calm pace is about 1.7 words a second, roughly 10 s), so length can only come from delivery and pauses. A TTS model treats 'fit 10 seconds' loosely. I would not rely on the instruction alone. Today I would split the script one sentence per line with a write node, so voice.js synthesises each sentence separately and the per-clip lead and tail silences become natural pauses, and I would ask explicitly for a slow, unhurried pace. The proper fix is the harness conforming the voice to the asked length by lengthening the pauses between sentences.

evidence from the files
assets/calm_voiceover.mp3: mono 24 kHz MP3, 7.80 s, peak -13.6 dB, mean -32.4 dB. silencedetect: lead 0–0.49 s, speech 0.49–1.84 s, pause 0.90 s, speech 2.74–4.28 s, pause 0.74 s, speech 5.02–7.14 s, tail 0.64 s. That is three sentences, about 5.0 s of speech. The exec log shows voice.js received the exact script. The judge's transcript matched it, and only the length check failed (7.8 s against about 10). The grader is right: 22% short of an explicitly requested length.

Fix voice.js: honour params.seconds. After synthesis, if the speech is shorter than 90% of the target, detect the pauses between sentences (silencedetect) and lengthen them evenly, capped at about 2 s each, with any remainder as a short tail, until the file is within ±5% of the target. If it is longer than 110%, re-synthesise with a faster-pace instruction or report it. Also derive the pace instruction from the words-per-second needed. Note: gpt-4o-mini-tts ignores the 'speed' parameter, so code must do the timing. Separately, the voice-gender regex matches 'other' as 'her' and 'manner' or 'human' as 'man'; match whole words.

Two Voices Trading Short Lines

23

Can you make one audio-only clip, around 8 seconds, with two clearly different voices? Friendly, natural conversation. A is a lower voice, B is a higher voice. Read only the lines, not the labels: A: Ready to go? B: Almost. Have you got the tickets? A: Right here. B: Great, let's go! No music or sound effects.

broke at: Executor voice + grader Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent's plan is right: one voice step with the four 'A:/B:' lines (labels select speakers and are not read), voice hints in extra. The voice tool then assigned the voices backwards. It picks the first speaker's voice with /female|woman|her\b/ on extra, and the agent's extra contained 'B higher;', where 'higher' ends in 'her', so A got coral (a higher female voice) and B got onyx (a low male voice), the opposite of 'A lower, B higher'. All four lines were spoken; the judge's claim that B's lines are missing comes from the transcript, not the audio. The agent could not have known that words like 'higher' steer the voice choice. Knowing the code, I would write extra so the first speaker resolves to the low voice ('voice: male') and leave out 'higher' or 'her'.

evidence from the files
dialogue.mp3 is 7.08 s, mono 24 kHz. silencedetect finds speech at 0-0.82, 1.48-2.03, 2.76-3.86, 4.13-4.70, 5.56-5.78 and 6.39-7.08 s, matching 'Ready to go?' / 'Almost.' 'Have you got the tickets?' / 'Right here.' / 'Great,' 'let's go!'. Autocorrelation pitch per segment: A's lines ~226 and ~238 Hz, B's lines ~98-112 Hz: B is the LOW voice, reversed from the request. All segments are at similar level (RMS -19.6 to -27.1 dB), so B's lines are audible, not missing as the judge's transcript implied. The tool note reads '4 line(s), 7 s, voices coral, onyx'.

Fix Harness (tools/voice.js): 1) match voice words with real word boundaries (\bher\b, \bfemale\b, \bmale\b), so 'higher' or 'other' does not pick a voice; 2) better, parse per-speaker hints from extra ('A: lower/deep/male', 'B: higher/bright/female') and map lower to onyx/ash and higher to coral/nova, falling back to label order; 3) send each line its own speaker's instructions rather than the whole extra; 4) read the result back (transcribe and compare per line) and redo once on a wrong or missing line. Grader: align the transcript against detected speech segments (or transcribe per segment) before declaring lines missing; here the transcriber returned only the two high-voice lines although all six speech bursts are present at similar level.

Twenty Second Podcast Intro

32

Make a 20-second audio intro for my podcast, Small Wonders. A warm female voice should say: “Welcome to Small Wonders, the show about big ideas hiding in everyday life. I'm Maya. Let's get curious.” Put upbeat, gentle electronic music underneath, with a little music-only opening and a smooth fade at the end. One finished audio file, please.

broke at: Executor assemble + agent-reasoning Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The ingredients were right: exact script, warm synthetic female voice (9.1 s), a 20 s gentle electronic bed, and one sounds-only assemble with a clear brief ("voice starts at 2 seconds... duck music beneath speech... fade from 16 to 20"). The mix is where it failed. assemble's sounds-only path keeps the FIRST input at full level and puts every other input at 0.25. It reads no offsets or ducking from extra, and the length follows the first input. The agent listed the music first, so the music played at full level and the voice sat about 20 dB under it, starting at 0 s with no music-only opening. The catalogue promises "music under speech, not over it" and never mentions the ordering rule, so the agent had no way to know. The transcriber caught only a garbled scrap of the buried voice ('Keeping ideas and morale high', most likely 'big ideas hiding in everyday life'). I would put the voice first, and the opening and ducking need assemble to support them.

evidence from the files
intro_voice.mp3 (9.1 s) holds the exact script; intro_music.mp3 is 20 s. In small_wonders_intro.mp3 the half-second RMS matches the music alone exactly (-13 to -21 dB) for the whole 20 s. The voice, mixed at 0.25, sits at about -36 to -48 dB, roughly 20 dB under the music, and starts at 0 s. assemble.js uses `volume=${k ? 0.25 : 1}` with `duration=first` and no offsets. The judge is right that the intro is not clearly spoken.

Fix Rework assemble's sounds-only mix. (1) Put the input that came from voice on top whatever its position; never infer this from order. (2) Loudness-normalise: voice at about -16 LUFS, the bed 12–15 dB under it while speech plays (sidechain ducking) and at full level otherwise. (3) Honour "voice at: N" offsets and a fade length. (4) Take the total length from params.seconds. Until then, state the order rule in the catalogue. This applies to every podcast intro, audiogram or voice-over mix.

Tiny Forests Two Host Segment

58

Turn this article into a roughly 90-second podcast chat between two hosts. Use two clearly different English voices, one male and one female, friendly and curious rather than newsreader-ish. Explain what tiny urban forests are and discuss the article's main points without making up facts. No music. Please give me the finished audio, not just a script.

broke at: Grader + harness Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The plan is what I would run: write, with article.txt as context, a two-speaker script in 'Name: line' form at about 2.5 words a second, then voice it with two distinct synthetic voices. No music, no assemble. The script holds every main point of the article (Miyawaki's method, 3-5 native saplings per m² in enriched soil, competition for light, about 3 years to self-sustain, cooler streets, insects and birds, schoolchildren, thin evidence, sapling die-off, not a substitute for large trees that store more carbon). It invents nothing: 'Akira Miyawaki' and 'three to five saplings' are both in the article. One host asks and reacts while the other explains. The only thing I would change is the prompt, asking for looser paraphrase and more reactions from both hosts, because Maya's lines are close to verbatim article sentences. The failure is the grader's. Its transcript stopped about 25 s in ('in enriched'), and it was never given the article, so every content check became cannot_tell. It then called the truncation a 'major fault' of the audio, but the file has continuous speech to 99.8 s. One harness quirk did not affect the grade: voice.js picks the first voice from the word 'female' in extra, so 'Alex' (meant male) got the female 'coral' voice and 'Maya' got the male 'onyx'. That is still one male and one female voice, but the reverse of the plan.

evidence from the files
The article (126 words) and podcast_script.txt (231 words, 14 alternating Alex/Maya lines) match point for point, with no invented facts. tiny_urban_forests_podcast.mp3 is 99.8 s, mono 24 kHz, with RMS between -22 and -34 dB in every 5 s window. silencedetect shows only inter-turn pauses of 0.3-1.9 s and speech right to the end, so there is no truncation at 'in enriched' (about 22-25 s in). The voice note says 'voices coral, onyx': one female, one male. The judge's verdicts are all cannot_tell, apart from length = yes, and its single major fault is about its own partial transcript.

Fix Grader: transcribe the whole file, not just the first ~25 s, and give the judge the user's attachments (article.txt) when a must-have checks facts against them. Never raise a 'major fault' from the grader's own truncated evidence. Harness: voice.js should map speakers to voices from per-name hints in extra ('Alex: male', 'Maya: female') or from a known-name gender guess, rather than taking the first match of 'female' anywhere in extra.

Five Tips Five Separate Slides

52

Need a 4:5 Instagram carousel: five focus tips, one per slide. Use these in order: 'Clear your desk', 'Silence notifications', 'Pick one task', 'Set a timer', 'Take a short break'. Number them 1–5, with a small matching illustration on each. Clean blue-and-white design. No extra cover or closing slide.

broke at: Planner + model-limit Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The structure was right: five qwen nodes, one per tip, exact words quoted, numbered, no cover. The agent dropped the one explicit design instruction, 'Clean blue-and-white design'. None of the five prompts contains the word blue. The planner prompt has a rule for exactly this ('THE USER'S WORDS ARE THE SPEC: their colours … go into the prompt as they said them'), and A03d dropped 'black-and-cream' the same way. It also asked for consistency only in extra ('use the same layout and typography as the other slides'). Each image node is generated independently, so that sentence means nothing: qwen gave five different type weights, numeral sizes and line placements. I would write one fully specified template (palette with a hex, numeral position and size, headline font and weight, illustration style and position, margins) and paste it verbatim into all five prompts, changing only the number, the tip and the illustration subject. I would set aspect 4:5 on the image node itself so the harness PADS the lettered square rather than cutting it: the agent's centre crop left 'Pick one task' and 'Take a short break' almost touching the edges. The catalogue line ('other sizes are cut from these by code') hides that pad path.

evidence from the files
The five slides are 512x640, centre-cut from 640x640 qwen renders. All are black or dark grey on white with no blue anywhere. Numerals and headlines change weight and size from slide to slide: slide 4 is light, slide 5's numeral is oversized, and 'Pick one task' and 'Take a short break' run nearly edge to edge after the crop. Tips, order, numbering and illustrations (desk, muted phone, checkbox, timer, person stretching) are all correct. The agent's five prompts never mention blue. The judge's major fault (no blue) and minor fault (inconsistent typography) match the images, so the grader is right.

Fix Add a code guard in plan.js guard(), next to the existing STYLE guard. Extract the colour words the user stated ('blue-and-white', 'black and cream', '#1F2A44') from the sheet and prepend 'Colours: <their words>.' to every image or image-edit prompt that lacks them. Add a planner rule for sets (carousel, pack, series): write one template paragraph and repeat it verbatim in every node, varying only the item. Change the catalogue line under image to say that a lettered design with params.aspect 4:5 is padded, not cut, so the planner sets the aspect on the image node rather than adding a crop.

One Print Style Across Plants

34

Make four square Instagram carousel slides: Monstera, Snake plant, Pothos, Peace lily, in that order. One plant and its name per slide. Keep the exact same sage-green-and-cream linocut style throughout: same border, lettering, paper texture and pot shape. Only the plant and name should change. Send separate slides.

broke at: Planner + harness + model-limit Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent made four independent qwen generations and its prompts dropped most of the user's spec: no 'sage-green-and-cream' palette, no pot, no paper texture, no border or lettering description. It relied on the words 'same border style' and 'simple consistent layout', which mean nothing to four separate generations that never see each other. The style guard then prefixed a garbled capture of the user's sentence ('In a linocut style throughout: same border style:'). Each slide invented its own border, font, ink colour (three black, one green) and none drew a pot. For a carousel that must share an exact template I would design slide 1 with every shared element spelled out, then make slides 2-4 as edits of slide 1 that swap only the plant and the name. An edit carries the border, paper, pot and lettering over; a new generation does not.

evidence from the files
The four 640x640 slides are spelled correctly and in order, and the plants are recognisable. But 01_monstera has a patterned black border, black ink and sans lettering; 02_snake_plant a rough black frame, black ink and sans lettering; 03_pothos no border, green watercolour-like foliage and serif lettering; 04_peace_lily a double-line frame, black ink and serif lettering. No slide has a pot, none is sage green on cream. The prompts sent were 'In a linocut style throughout: same border style: Instagram carousel slide featuring one <plant>...', with no palette, pot or paper; the 'In a linocut style throughout: same border style:' prefix came from the style guard.

Fix 1) Planner rule and catalogue CHOOSING line: 'A SET THAT SHARES ONE DESIGN (carousel, series, menu cards, event pack): make the first piece with every shared element spelled out (palette, border, lettering, paper, recurring objects), then each other piece as an image-edit OF THE FIRST that changes only the variable part (parallel, from the same master); never N independent generations.' 2) Add to image POORLY: 'the same border, font or layout across separate generations'. 3) Harness style guard: stop the capture at ':' as well as ',;.', keep the user's colour words with the style ('sage-green-and-cream linocut'), and do not prefix when the prompt already leads with the style. 4) A pre-run check: every colour word and named object in the sheet's quotes must appear in each image prompt (the palette and the pot were dropped).

Kitchen Renovation Side by Side

48

Put these kitchen photos side by side in one landscape 16:9 image. Old kitchen on the left, renovated one on the right, labeled “Before” and “After”. Keep both photos as they are, just fit them neatly.

broke at: Executor planner rules Claude's fix would pass: yes

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent's plan is the right one and the same as mine: compose (code), the before photo first, labels Before and After, 16:9, fit: contain, nothing redrawn. The fault was in compose's label parser at run time: "labels: Before, After" was taken as a single label, and that label went onto the first panel only, so one box reading "Before, After" sits over the old kitchen and the new one has none. compose.js was edited three minutes after this run (output 05:55:13, file 05:58:00). It now splits labels on "|" or ",", and drops a label list whose count does not match the pictures, so the same plan would now label each panel.

evidence from the files
kitchen-before-after.png is 1280x720. The brown-cabinet kitchen is on the left and the white-cabinet kitchen on the right, both whole and unstretched on a neutral ground. One grey label box reading 'Before, After' sits above the left panel only; the right panel has none. The run note says 'labelled Before, After', and the current code would print 'Before / After'. The judge is right.

Fix The fix is already in the working tree: compose splits labels on '|' or ',' and requires one label per picture. Add a regression test with 'labels: Before, After', and keep the catalogue example 'labels: Before | After'. This covers every labelled compose.

Imagine My Kitchen Renovation

44

Can you show how my kitchen could look renovated? Make one 16:9 before-and-after image, original on the left and your realistic makeover on the right. White shaker cabinets, light oak counters, white subway tiles, no clutter. Keep the same room layout and camera angle. Label them “Before” and “After”.

broke at: Planner + model-limit Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The structure was right, and it is mine. One image-edit of the user's photo on klein keeps the room layout (qwen would reframe it). Then the code compose puts the untouched original beside it with exact 'Before'/'After' labels at 16:9. The two failures trace to the edit prompt. First, it said 'remove all clutter' without saying what clutter is. klein took the taps, the second sink on the right-hand counter and the rear sink's faucet as clutter and erased them, which broke the 'major fixture positions' must-have. Second, 'white subway tiles' was never described as a shape. klein, faithful to the existing square grid, re-coloured the square tiles white. An expert writing an edit prompt says exactly what must survive (both sinks with their taps, the window, the sockets, the appliance) and which loose items count as clutter. It describes the target finish concretely (3:1 rectangles in a staggered brick bond). The planner rule 'for an edit, say what must stay unchanged' was followed only generically ('preserve the room layout').

evidence from the files
kitchen-before.jpg (640x384) has brown cabinets, square beige tiles, a steel sink with tap under the upper cabinets, and a second double sink with tap on the right counter over a white unit. kitchen-after.png (640x384, klein, 5 cr) has white shaker doors and light oak counters, keeps the geometry and viewpoint, and clears the counters. But the right-hand double sink and its tap became plain oak counter, the rear sink has no tap, and the tiles are a white square grid matching the old layout. The final 1280x720 compose shows the untouched original left and the edit right under readable 'Before'/'After' labels. The judge's two failures are accurate.

Fix Planner prompt rule for clean-ups and renovations by image-edit: 'never write remove all clutter or tidy up alone. List the loose items to remove, and name every fixture that must stay (sinks, taps, hob, window, sockets, appliances, doors) with where it is. Describe a requested finish by its shape and pattern (subway tile = 3:1 rectangle in a brick bond; shaker = flat recessed panel).' Optionally add a check node after the edit ('are both sinks and taps present in the same places?') that triggers one redo on failure.

broke at: Executor lettering read-back + model-limit + agent-reasoning Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The plan shape matches the catalogue rule I would follow too: one lettered image per size from the same brief, not crops. Square and portrait came out right. The landscape's first qwen render had all five strings but two were garbled ('20% off n / all indoor plants', 'Saturday, 8. Sunday') because all five lines were squeezed into a half-width column of a 640x360 canvas. The harness's one fix then made it strictly worse. Its prompt asked qwen to 'read exactly "20% off all indoor plants"' while also 'remove the Discount block, first line … entirely' and 'remove … second line … entirely'. qwen deleted the discount and wrote 'Saturday & Sunday' where it had been, the garbled date stayed, and nobody re-read the result before the node was marked done. My prompts would differ in two ways. They would state the user's 'green-and-cream' (the agent's three prompts never mention a colour, and the palette came out right only by luck) and give each shape an explicit layout: in 16:9, the text panel takes two-thirds of the width with one short line per string, so the type stays large. The decisive defect is the fix step, the same one that sank A03d.

evidence from the files
fern_house_square.png (640x640): all five lines correct and readable, green serif on near-white, leaves around the edges. fern_house_portrait.png (360x640): all five correct, with the address small but legible. fern_house_landscape-before-text-fix.png (640x360): text in the left half; '20% off n' / 'all indoor plants' and a garbled small 'Saturday, 8. Sunday'. The other lines are correct. fern_house_landscape.png after the fix: the discount line is gone, 'Saturday & Sunday' sits in its place, and the garbled date line remains below it. exec.json shows the fix prompt mixing 'read exactly' with 'remove … entirely' for the same block, plus 'people, faces, poses, hands' boilerplate. The judge's two major faults match exactly, so the grader is right.

Fix Same harness fix as A03d, in execute.js and buildable.js fixText. A garbled rendering of a WANTED string is a misspelling to correct in place, never a 'stray' to remove; fixText must not send 'remove … entirely' for something it is also asked to write. Fix one string per edit, naming its position. Re-read after the fix, with up to 2 rounds, and choose between the before and after images by the readback: here the 'before' had 5 of 5 strings present, the 'after' 4. Flag the node instead of reporting 'lettering fixed' when it still misreads. Also add a palette guard so the user's stated colours enter every image prompt (see G34b).

Rescheduled Event Across All Formats

37

Make a matching 4:5 poster, vertical story image and 10-second vertical reel for Rooftop Jazz. Put these details on each: 17 October 2027 / 7 PM / Atlas Roof / Free entry. Go with a cream-and-burgundy jazz-club look. / We've moved it to 24 October 2027. Update all three, including every place the date appears in the reel. Keep everything else the same and send the revised pack.

broke at: Planner + harness Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The two still revisions were right (qwen edits with lettering: 24 October 2027 in place, everything else kept). For the reel the agent asked text-overlay to 'reproduce the existing overlays, replacing every occurrence of "17 October 2027" with "24 October 2027"' and passed the old reel as a 'reference'. text-overlay is a renderer, not an editor: it cannot read old overlays, it only draws the words it is given. The harness takes every quoted string in the instruction as the words, so it drew '17 October 2027' over '24 October 2027' at the default bottom position and nothing else. The reference input was ignored. I would re-overlay the clean base clip (rooftop_reel_base.mp4) with the COMPLETE new text, one quoted string per line, at the same top position for the whole 10 s. That also fixes the turn-1 reel, whose card showed literal '\n' because the agent wrote '\n' inside one quoted string.

evidence from the files
rooftop_poster_4x5_revised.png (512x640) and rooftop_story_revised.png (352x640) are faithful edits: same layout and illustration, '24 October 2027 / 7 PM / Atlas Roof / Free entry' and 'Rooftop Jazz' exact, no old date. rooftop_reel_revised.mp4 (720x1280, 10.03 s) shows only a bottom card reading '17 October 2027' above '24 October 2027' over the clean base footage, with no event name, time or place. The turn-1 rooftop_reel.mp4 card at the top read 'Rooftop Jazz\n17 October 2027 / 7 PM\nAtlas Roof / Free entry' with literal \n. execute.js builds overlay text as quoted.join('\n') from prompt_or_change.

Fix 1) Catalogue/planner: text-overlay 'draws exactly the words you give it; it cannot read or edit earlier overlays: to change a word, re-overlay the clean clip with the complete new text'. 2) Harness: when the instruction holds quoted strings joined by 'replace/with/instead of', do not render them all; take only the replacement, or refuse with 'text-overlay needs the full text'. Convert a literal backslash-n in the text to a line break. Reject a second clip input instead of ignoring it. 3) Keep the clean base of every overlaid clip in the session (it was, as rooftop_reel_base.mp4) and have the planner prefer it for revisions.

The white listing image is the input of the other two, so it was never shown to the judge, who then failed 'three images', 'same mug' and 'whole mug on white' for a picture that exists and is correct. Where I differ from the agent: a zoom-2 crop of a 640 px image is only 320x320 and soft, so I would upscale it (25 cr). Until deliverables are explicit, I would also give the listing shot its own end node.

evidence from the files
mug_white.png (640x640) shows the whole sage-green mug, handle on the right, on pure white, with no text: a correct listing shot. mug_breakfast.png shows the same mug on linen on a wooden table in window light. mug_rim_closeup.png (320x320) shows the rim and glaze and is soft. 'Final outputs' lists only the last two. deliverables() in grade.mjs filters out consumed outputs and only re-adds text-overlay, crop, place and assemble outputs in packs.

Fix Make deliverables explicit. Give plan steps a `deliver: true` flag (plan2.js already lists deliverables; carry them into the plan) and have grade.mjs deliverables() and the UI use it. Failing that, in a pack, count any picture or clip output whenever the sinks are fewer than spec.outputs. This affects every pack whose first piece seeds the rest (a hero shot reused for variants, a poster reused for a reel).

G39b

Monday Meme From Scratch

90

make a meme about Mondays

broke at: Planner + harness Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The finished meme is good: the judge passed all five must-haves, and I agree. The only failure is the question 'What style or mood?' before starting. 'Make a meme about Mondays' is a low-stakes, conventional format. Its style is the meme convention itself (a reaction photo plus bold outlined caption), and an expert would just pick a joke and an image. The question did not come from the planner's judgment but from the sheet's policy. The sheet prompt makes direction 'needed' unless tone, style or message is given or the user says 'your call'. sheet.js then asks the image branch's style field whenever direction=needed and style is unknown. Nothing in that policy recognises formats whose look is implied (meme, sticker, thumbnail, emoji) or a casual one-line request. So the agent asked the question that, as the answer sheet shows, nearly every user answers with 'your call'. After the answer, the plan (write the caption, then one lettered qwen image with the caption fed in as exact words) is exactly what I would run.

evidence from the files
Final monday_meme.png is 640x640: a tabby cat lying flat with half-closed eyes, captioned in bold white letters with black outline, 'Monday started. My cat has requested five more business naps.', all inside the frame. The judge scored all 5 must-haves yes. The only failed check is 'asks nothing' = [style: 'What style or mood?'], and the user answered 'your call'. The note shows the first qwen pass had stray garbled lettering, which the harness's one fix removed. The picture is a 16:9 image padded top and bottom to 1:1.

Fix In sheet.js, stop asking style or mood by default. Treat it like kind, audience and size: infer it. Ask only when the user's own brand or a high-stakes design is involved and nothing implies a look. At minimum, add to the sheet prompt: 'direction is free (not needed) when the format implies its own look (meme, sticker, emoji, reaction image, thumbnail) or the request is a casual one-liner; style is then inferred with confidence 1.' Harness side note: the lettering fix returned a 16:9 picture that finish() then padded to 1:1 with olive bands. The fix pass should be asked for the step's own aspect.

Black Bottle Product Reel

47

Make a 15-second vertical 9:16 ad for the bottle in my photo. Clean studio look, a few moving close-ups, mellow music, no talking. Start with “Your everyday bottle” and end with “Shop now”. Keep the bottle looking like mine.

broke at: Planner + grader + missing-tool Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The tree is the right shape: studio stills edited from the user's photo, three 5 s image-to-video shots, a 15 s music bed, assemble, and two code text-overlays. Two of the three faults were written into the agent's own prompts. (1) The closing still asked klein for 'clear space below for a closing caption'. klein, which the catalogue says 'misspells and invents text', painted a caption ('Ridectarp dehaime bultae dliy') that sits under the overlaid 'Shop now' for the last 3 s. (2) Every still and clip prompt said to preserve the bottle's 'existing label' or 'markings', but the bottle is plain matte black with no label. Asking a model to keep a label that isn't there invites one, and the hero push-in grew a large white 'BMOOY' wordmark around 3–4 s. The agent never sees the photo, only its filename, so it assumed a label. I would describe the product as plain on every side, never mention captions or text space in a picture prompt (the overlay adds the words afterwards), and use camera moves rather than product rotation. The third fault, spoken Korean ('여러분 안녕하세요!' = 'Hello everyone!'), can only have come from the music track, because all three shots are silent. The track's spectrogram shows only steady chord stacks and percussive hits, with no speech formants or gliding pitch contours, and that phrase is a classic speech-to-text hallucination on music. So it is most likely a grader artefact (gpt-4o-transcribe on an instrumental bed) rather than real vocals. Nothing in our system can listen to check either way.

evidence from the files
bottle-closing.png (640x640, klein edit) has garbled black text 'Ridectarp dehaime bultae dliy' painted at the bottom, and the frame at 13.5 s shows it under the 'Shop now' band. A 1 fps strip shows a large white 'BMOOY' wordmark and small print appearing on the bottle around 3–4 s of shot 1, which the source photo does not have. shot-01/02/03.mp4 are 270x480, 5.17 s, video only (silent), so the only audio in bottle-ad-final.mp4 is mellow-music.mp3 (15 s, peak -1 dB). Its spectrogram (0–5 kHz) shows sustained chord harmonics under 1.2 kHz and percussive transients, with no speech-like formant movement. The 'spoken Korean' is therefore probably a transcription hallucination, and that one fault is probably wrong. The opening and closing overlays are exact. The bottle's shape and loop are preserved. The overall fail is still right, because the garbled caption and invented wordmark are real.

Fix (1) Planner PROMPTS rule: never ask a picture or clip model to leave room for, or keep, words ('space for a caption', 'its label') unless they exist. Words added later by overlay are not mentioned to the model, and a supplied product is described as it is ('plain, no label or text'). (2) Feed the planner a one-line vision caption of each supplied picture in MATERIALS ('product-bottle.jpg: plain matte black bottle, no label, on a wooden table'), so it stops assuming labels. (3) Grader: run a voice-activity or music-versus-speech check before trusting a transcript of a music bed. A lone stock phrase on an instrumental track ('여러분 안녕하세요', 'Thank you for watching') should count as a probable hallucination, not 'speech heard'. Harness: the same audio probe as E24c, run on generated music to regenerate genuine vocals. (4) Make each image-to-video's 'no text' explicit by code when the source is plain.

Candle Ad Without Photos

52

I don't have a photo. Make a 15-second 9:16 ad for a candle: clear straight-sided glass jar, ivory wax, one wick, no label. Warm evening light, gentle camera moves and soft piano, no voice. Show “A little evening calm”, then finish with “Find your glow”.

broke at: Grader Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent's plan is the one I would run: one product still (so the jar is the same in every shot), three gentle 5 s image-to-video moves from it, a 15 s solo-piano bed, one assemble at 9:16 / 15 s, and two timed code overlays with the exact lines (0-5 s and 10-15 s). The clips' invented sound was dropped, so the only audio is the piano. The single failing finding, 'speech: 여름이야기', is a transcription hallucination on solo piano, not something the agent did. My only optional refinements: a short dissolve between shots (not asked for) and the closing line held to the very end, which it already is.

evidence from the files
candle_ad_final.mp4: 720x1280, 15.03 s, hard cuts at 5.03 and 10.03 s; frames show the same clear straight-sided glass jar, ivory wax, one wick, no label, warm lamplight; 'A little evening calm' (0-5 s) and 'Find your glow' (10-15 s) exact at the top. shot_1-3.mp4 have no audio stream, so the only sound is soft_piano.mp3 (15 s PCM, mixed at full level; final peak -0.8 dB). Its 0-4 kHz spectrogram shows only piano: sharp onsets with flat, decaying harmonics, no gliding or formant-shaped vocal energy. The judge's sole failing point was the transcript '여름이야기' ('summer story'), a hallucination on instrumental audio.

Fix Grader: stop treating the transcriber's output as proof of speech. gpt-4o-transcribe returns short random-language fragments on instrumental music ('여름이야기' here, '끄덕끄덕' and 'Dieu, tu es grand' on D20a, 'Sustantivo femenino.' on -91 dB silence in H41c). Before telling the judge 'speech heard', require a voice-activity/vocal detector (or a second transcription that agrees, with a prompt allowing an empty result), drop transcripts under ~5 words that are in a language other than the item's, and pass the result to the judge as 'possible speech (unverified)' rather than a fact.

Sneaker Captions Stay Safely Inside

37

Make a silent 15-second 9:16 sneaker ad. No photo—use a plain white leather low-top with white laces and a white sole, no logo. Three moving shots, with these captions in order: “Meet your everyday pair”, “Clean look. Easy style.”, “Shop now”. Keep all captions at least 15% in from either side and 20% from the top and bottom so reel buttons won't cover them.

broke at: Executor text-overlay + agent-reasoning Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

Most of the plan is mine too: a generated plain white sneaker, two flux edits for detail and profile views, three 5 s image-to-video shots, one silent assemble at 15 s, then code captions in the safe area. The failure is the last node. The agent put all three captions into one text-overlay, with "caption 1 from: 0; to: 5; caption 2 from: 5; to: 10; caption 3 from: 10; to: 15" in extra. The executor joined every quoted string in the prompt with newlines into ONE card, and text-overlay.js reads only the first "from:"/"to:" pair. So all three captions appear stacked for 0–5 s and nothing appears after that. The agent stretched a format the tool does not parse (in H42a it correctly used one node per caption), but the tool merged them silently instead of honouring the windows or refusing. I would chain three text-overlay nodes, one caption and one window each, all at middle.

evidence from the files
Grader frame at 1.9 s: all three captions are stacked in one grey band ('Meet your everyday pair / Clean look. Easy style. / Shop now'). Frames at 5.6, 9.4 and 13.1 s: no caption. In exec.json the text-overlay prompt is 'Meet your everyday pair\nClean look. Easy style.\nShop now', and text-overlay.js reads only the first 'from'/'to' (0–5 s). The sneaker views are consistent: white, no logo. The judge is right.

Fix Change text-overlay so that when the prompt holds N quoted captions and extra holds N from/to windows (or "caption k from:"), it renders one card per caption for its own window. Today the executor joins all quotes into one card and the tool uses only the first window. Otherwise it should refuse, so the planner chains nodes. Add the planner rule "one text-overlay node per timed caption" and expose a size or max-width so safe-area margins can be met. This covers every timed caption or subtitle sequence.

FitTrack Ad From Supplied Screenshots

40

Make a 10-second widescreen 16:9 ad for FitTrack using both screenshots. Show the home screen first, then the workout screen, and finish with the app name. Clean, energetic, with an upbeat instrumental beat and no voiceover. Other copy is your call.

broke at: Planner + harness + grader Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

This is the same mistake as D20d. The agent fed the two portrait screenshots (720x1280) straight into assemble and wrote 'fit screenshots without cropping or stretching on a clean neutral background' into extra. assemble never reads that: it always fills the 16:9 frame and centre-crops, which keeps only the middle third of each phone screen. The 'FitTrack' and 'Workout' headers and the first and last rows were lost. The catalogue's CHOOSING line ('Keep ALL of a picture in a new size, crop with fit: contain') covers this exactly, and assemble's guarantee 'the user's photos used as they are' misled it. Second divergence: 'finish with the app name' is an end card. The catalogue routes title and end cards to an image node with lettering true. The agent instead laid a small plain text-overlay band over the last 2 s of the cropped workout screen (the judge's 'weak, cluttered brand finish'). I would contain-fit each screenshot on a plain background in its own header colour, add a lettered 'FitTrack' end card as a third piece, lay a 10 s instrumental beat under it, and let assemble cut the three in order. The 'speech' verdict ('すべての人に') looks like a transcription artefact: the beat's spectrogram shows fixed-pitch synth stabs, not vocal formants. I cannot rule out a vocal chop without listening.

evidence from the files
app-home.png and app-workout.png are 720x1280 mock screens with a blue 'FitTrack' header and green 'Workout' header over grey row labels. In fittrack-ad-final.mp4 frames at 1 fps, each screen is cover-cropped to its middle: only 'Workout 32 min / Sleep 7 h 10 min / Water...' and 'Squats / Push-ups / Plank...' are visible, with headers and top and bottom rows cut. A small 'FitTrack' band appears over the workout crop at 8-10 s. fittrack-beat.mp3 is 10.0 s. Its 100-4000 Hz spectrogram shows rhythmic fixed-pitch synth chords from 2 s on, with no gliding vocal formants. assemble.js has no contain path.

Fix Same fix as D20d, which generalises to every reel or ad built from supplied photos or screenshots. (1) Correct assemble's catalogue guarantee: it crops pictures to fill and pushes in, so a whole picture needs crop fit: contain first. (2) Make assemble honour 'fit: contain' in extra and switch off the 8% push-in on contained pictures; otherwise the top header of a contained portrait screenshot gets shaved by up to 3.7%. (3) Planner guard: a supplied picture whose aspect differs from the target by more than 10% gets a crop fit:contain before assemble unless the user asked for a crop. (4) Planner: 'finish with the name or logo' becomes an end-card image node with lettering true, not a text-overlay. (5) Grader: confirm a speech claim on a music bed with a vocal-presence check before failing.

Service Ad Without Source Assets

58

Make an 8-second 16:9 ad for ClearDay, a made-up app that turns a messy to-do list into a simple daily plan. I don't have screenshots or a logo—create a simple demo screen yourself. Show the messy list becoming an organized day, then end on ClearDay. Calm blue-and-white look, no sound. Any other wording is up to you.

broke at: Planner + model-limit + harness Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent knew klein misspells, so it tried to dodge text: a demo screen 'with checkbox icons and abstract blue lines instead of written words', on klein with lettering off. That failed twice. klein still painted a garbled header ('DyVmning') and section labels ('Dsure Ensues'), as the catalogue warns it 'invents text'. And a to-do app whose tasks are blue strokes is not a credible demo, which is the judge's major fault. An app screen is a designed piece whose words carry the meaning, so I would make both demo states on qwen with lettering on and short real task names, quoted so the readback checks them. Because the catalogue says image-to-video 'CANNOT: readable text inside the motion', I would not morph lettered cards. I would show the change as a before/after inside one assemble: messy state, organised state (an image-edit of the messy one on qwen, so the style matches), then a designed ClearDay end card. The cut shows the transformation with every word exact. The agent also asked text-overlay for 'navy text on a white band'. The tool cannot do that (white text on a fixed translucent dark box), so it produced the dark-grey slab the judge called disconnected; a lettered end card avoids it.

evidence from the files
messy_tasks.png (640x360, klein) and organized_day.png (640x384, klein edit; the b2 harness did not crop edits) both show a white phone panel headed by a garbled 'DyVmning' with garbled section labels and blue strokes for tasks. The 1 fps grid of clearday_ad.mp4 (858x480, 8.0 s) shows the scattered cards gliding into a timeline, which is a real transformation, and the overlay 'ClearDay' in white on a dark-grey box over the bottom of the panel from 6 s. The judge's major fault (garbled headings, strokes instead of tasks) and minor fault (dark slab) are both visible, so the grader is right.

Fix (1) Planner rule: a UI, app screen, dashboard, menu or chart mock-up is DESIGNED LETTERING. It goes on qwen with lettering true and short real words, never klein with 'no words' (klein invents them anyway). (2) Catalogue line under image-to-video: 'a before/after of a lettered screen is two lettered pictures cut together in assemble, not a morph'. (3) text-overlay: honour the colour and band asked for in extra (color, box: none, band colour), or reject the instruction so the planner knows. Today 'navy text on a white band' silently became white on dark grey.

Exact Copy App Ad

72

Create a silent 9-second 16:9 ad for my fictional planning app DayNest. Three equal-length scenes with these exact lines, one per scene in this order: 'Less scrolling. More doing.' / 'Plan your day in one place.' / 'Try DayNest today.' Keep capitals and punctuation exactly. No other visible words, even in the background. Use simple animated calendar and checkmark shapes on cream and green.

broke at: Grader + harness + model-limit Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent's plan is sound and nearly mine: three text-free cream-and-green stills, each animated for 3 s, assembled to 9 s at 16:9, and the three exact lines laid on by code, one per scene. Everything requested is there. Two nits I would do differently: (1) not mention 'a later caption' in the image prompts; I would say 'the bottom third of the frame is empty cream background', because 'clear area for a caption' produced a pale stripe behind the scene-2 caption, and the scene-2 animation was not told to keep its checkmarks inside the calendar, so three big checkmarks swept over the caption at ~5.6 s; (2) ask for no audio track at all. The fail itself came from the judge marking it 'not usable' after the transcriber 'heard' Spanish words in a -91 dB digital-silence track.

evidence from the files
daynest_ad.mp4: 1280x720, 9.03 s, cuts at 3.03 and 6.03 s (three equal scenes). Frames show green calendar tiles, a checkmarked calendar and a calendar with one large checkmark on cream; captions 'Less scrolling. More doing.' (0-3 s), 'Plan your day in one place.' (3-6 s), 'Try DayNest today.' (6-9 s) are exact, white on a grey box; no other words anywhere. At ~5.6 s three large green checkmarks sweep across the scene-2 caption (minor clutter, still legible), and a pale stripe sits behind that caption. The audio track is digital silence: volumedetect mean -91.0 dB, max -91.0 dB; scene clips have no audio. The judge listed both faults as minor yet marked it not usable, citing 'speech: Sustantivo femenino.'

Fix 1) Grader: the same transcription guard as D20a/H40b. Here the 'speech' came from a track whose mean and peak are both -91 dB; never transcribe a track below about -60 dB peak, and treat it as silent. 2) Harness: when no sound is given and the user asked for silence, have assemble write no audio stream rather than an anullsrc track. 3) Planner wording rule (as in D23b): describe reserved space as 'empty background' in composition terms, never 'for a caption', and keep animated elements inside named bounds.

Café Reel From Owner Photos

45

These are photos of my café. Make a cosy 9-second vertical Instagram reel using all three, storefront first. Gentle movement, soft upbeat music, no talking. Put “Maple Street Café” at the start and “Your morning starts here” at the end.

broke at: Grader + model-limit Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The plan does almost everything the user asked. The storefront comes first, all three of the owner's photos are used, the exact opening and closing text are code overlays, there is a soft instrumental bed, and it runs 9 s vertical. The decisive 'fault', speech reading 'عالم الزلازل' in the soundtrack, is not in the file. The three minimax shots have no audio stream (code dropped it), and the reel's audio is the music alone, at the same levels. The music's spectrogram shows steady instrument partials and a regular beat with no vocal contours. The same transcriber also reported speech on the -91 dB silent tracks of D23c and H40c. The one real flaw is the motion. The agent asked minimax for "a subtle slow push-in" over 3 s, and the model ran the latte from cup-and-saucer to an extreme foam close-up. I would skip image-to-video here. assemble already gives every still a slow 8% push-in by code: gentle movement for 0 credits that keeps the owner's photos exactly, with no model sound to strip. The catalogue does not mention this, so the agent could not know.

evidence from the files
The three shots (480x858, 3.04 s) have no audio stream. maple-street-cafe-reel.mp4's audio has a mean of -17.3 dB against -17.1 dB for cafe-music.mp3, so the only sound is the music. The music's spectrogram shows flat instrument harmonics and percussive hits every ~0.6 s, with no gliding or vibrato contours. Grader frames: storefront with the striped awning, tables and an exact caption; latte at 3.4 s vs 5.6 s pushes from cup-and-saucer to a foam close-up (real but minor); pastries with the exact closing line.

Fix Grader: never pass a transcript of a music-only or silent track to the judge as 'speech heard'. First gate it on a speech-presence test (whisper-1 verbose_json no_speech_prob, or a VAD) and on the peak level, and label low-confidence output as a likely transcriber hallucination. Catalogue: add to assemble's line that "pictures get a slow push-in (gentle movement, 0 credits)", so 'gentle movement' of photos does not send the planner to image-to-video. The grader fix matters for every item with a music bed or silent audio.

Casual Talking Camera Testimonial

0

Make an 8-second vertical testimonial-style ad for FitTrack. A fictional woman in her 30s, filming herself at home, talks to camera: “FitTrack makes planning my workouts so easy. I finally have a routine that sticks.” Friendly and casual, with matching captions. Use a made-up presenter, not a real customer.

broke at: Planner + harness Claude's fix would pass: likely

Nothing made

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent sent an 8-second, one-person, one-shot talking-head ad to the six-stage film chain. Its reason was 'because the presenter speaks on camera'. It was obeying a misleading planner rule: film is never for an ad or a clip of 20 s or less, 'unless the user names ... characters on screen speaking their lines (then film wins, whatever the kind)'. The same prompt's catalogue has the direct path: 'A face that speaks → talking-photo', with voice for the exact words. An expert sees one fictional presenter, one fixed selfie framing, 14 exact words and 8 s. That is a still of the presenter, a synthetic voice reading the script verbatim, a talking-photo to make her speak, and exact captions laid on by code. The film chain also hands exact captions and timing to a pipeline the planner does not control. The bench records film plans without running them, so nothing was made and the item scored 0. Even when run, the film chain is built for stories over 20 s.

evidence from the files
The session has only prompts and session.json: no assets were made. bench/v1/run.mjs line 50 sets notRun = 'the plan uses the film chain; film is run one at a time, not in this pass'. The plan's own 'say' gives the reason: 'I'll use the film workflow because the presenter speaks on camera'. That echoes plan.js's exception for 'characters on screen speaking their lines'. C17b in this same batch shows talking-photo on the free tier giving a convincing speaking head from one still and a voice track.

Fix Rewrite the planner rule in plan.js. Today it reads '... or characters on screen speaking their lines (then film wins, whatever the kind)'. Make it: 'one presenter or one talking head speaking to camera in a single setting, 30 s or less (testimonial, UGC ad, announcement, greeting) is a tree: image (or the user's photo), then voice (the exact words), then talking-photo, then captions or text-overlay. Film is only for several characters or several scenes.' Add a price-aware guard: a film plan whose total is under 20 s with one character is re-planned as a tree. Catalogue: talking-photo WELL 'a presenter or testimonial to camera'. Harness side note: the bench pass records film plans unrun, so a wrong film choice costs the whole item.

Countdown Into Neon Night

40

Make an 8-second vertical ad for Neon Night, 12 September 2026 at The Foundry, Leeds. Start with a big 3, 2, 1 countdown, building electronic beats and flashing neon, then reveal the event name, date and venue. Hold that end card so I can read it. No talking.

broke at: Executor assemble + grader + model-limit Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent's design work was right and the cards came out perfect: a qwen '3' poster, then qwen edits of it for '2', '1' and the event card, all lettered exactly and consistent in style. It wrote the timing it wanted in assemble's extra: 'countdown_3 0–1 s; countdown_2 1–2 s; countdown_1 2–3 s; event_end_card 3–8 s'. assemble.js ignores that and gives 4 pictures 8/4 = 2 s each, so the cuts landed at 2, 4 and 6 s and the end card had only 2 s against the required 3 or more. Same defect as D23a and E29b. With today's tools I would build each piece at its own length first: three 1-second card clips and one 5-second end-card clip, each a one-picture assemble. Then I would join them with seconds 0 (own lengths) and extra 'music: full'. The flag is needed because the silent tracks on those clips would otherwise make assemble duck the music to 25% as if there were speech. The 'speech' fault is doubtful. The judge only reads a gpt-4o-transcribe transcript, which returned one Sinhala word ('පෙම්වතුන්') for an electronic bed whose spectrogram shows synth harmonics, a riser and a pitch-bend, which is typical ASR hallucination material. I also would not name 'countdown' or 'voices' in the music prompt, since negations can prime vocal samples.

evidence from the files
neon_night_ad.mp4 is 720x1280, 8.02 s, with audio. Scene cuts at 2.02, 4.02 and 6.02 s give 2 s per card, so the event card shows only 6–8 s, exactly the share = 8/4 rule. The cards (352x640) are correct and consistent: white 3, 2, 1 on black with cyan and pink chevron streaks that vary between cards, then 'Neon Night' / '12 September 2026' / 'The Foundry, Leeds', unclipped. electronic_build.mp3 is 8.0 s. Its spectrogram shows a low drone to 3.7 s, then a synth drop with steady harmonic stacks, a riser near 4.4 s and one pitch-bend near 7.2 s, and no speech formant pattern. The 'speech' is therefore doubtful. The judge is right that the end card is too short, so the fail stands.

Fix (1) Same assemble.js fix as D23a and E29b: per-piece durations from extra ('durations: 1,1,1,5' or the planner's 'X 0–1 s' wording). Also, a clip's silent track must not count as speech when deciding to duck music: check its loudness, not just whether an audio stream exists. (2) Optional harness sync: detect the music's main energy jump (the drop) and move the reveal cut onto it, so 'accents matching the numeral changes' is by construction. (3) Grader: gate transcripts of music beds with voice-activity detection. A single word in an unexpected language over an instrumental track is a probable hallucination.

H44c

Rooftop Jazz in Two Formats

47

I need the same 10-second Rooftop Jazz promo in 9:16 for Stories and 16:9 for a venue screen. Sunset rooftop, musicians playing, mellow jazz, no voiceover. Show 'Rooftop Jazz', '18 July 2026' and 'Sky Terrace, Manchester'. Make both versions fill the frame and keep all the text readable.

broke at: Planner + model-limit + grader Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent built one 16:9 master and centre-cropped it to 9:16, betting on its still prompt ('musicians grouped in the central third'). A 9:16 crop of 16:9 keeps only 32% of the width; the model spread four or five musicians across the whole frame and the push-in widened them further, so the vertical version cuts the right-hand guitarist through the face at ~1-4 s. The user asked for both versions to 'fill the frame', which rules out padding, so the only safe route for a group of people is a native composition per aspect: recompose the wide still as a vertical one (an image-edit keeps the same musicians and look) and animate each. That costs a second clip, the price of not cutting faces. The text and audio parts of the agent's plan were fine. The judge's other fault ('speech' in the portrait audio) is a transcription artefact: the 16:9 version carries the same music track and was not flagged.

evidence from the files
rooftop_jazz_16x9.mp4 (1280x720, 10 s): four or five musicians spread across the full width at sunset with the skyline; the three lines exact on a centre band. rooftop_jazz_9x16.mp4 (720x1284, 10 s) is a centre crop of that master: at 1.3 s the right-hand guitarist's arm and guitar are already cut by the right edge, and at 3.8 s the edge cuts through his head (the judge's frame, confirmed); the second shot (saxophonist close-up) fits. Both versions carry the same mellow_jazz track, yet only the portrait was transcribed as 'たべるのの。'.

Fix 1) Planner rule / CHOOSING line: 'Several aspect versions of footage with people (a band, a group, two speakers): make each aspect natively (image, then an image-edit recomposing it into the other aspect, then image-to-video for each); never centre-crop 16:9 to 9:16, which keeps a third of the width. Crop only when there is one centred subject.' 2) Catalogue crop POORLY: 'groups spread across a wide frame: a 9:16 crop of 16:9 cuts the people at the sides'. 3) After any crop of footage with people, run frame + check 'is any face cut by the frame edge?'. 4) Grader: the transcription guard (the same track was 'speech' in one version and clean in the other).

Make the First One Square

Make two tall 4:5 illustrations, no text. First: a fox sleeping under a crescent moon. Second: a lighthouse in a storm. Both soft watercolours. / Make the first one square instead. Keep the same art and make sure the fox and moon both fit.

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)
