The planner never saw "Both soft watercolours.": the sheet stored it only as the quote of direction=stated, and the planner prompt prints `direction: stated (stated)`. The newer style guard in plan.js would not have caught it either: its regex needs a word boundary right after 'watercolour', so the plurals 'watercolours' and 'illustrations' don't match. For turn 2 I would deliver the 1:1 picture the 4:5 was cut from. It is the same art, already square, with nothing padded or regenerated.

sleeping_fox_source.png (640x640) and sleeping_fox_square.png both show a photoreal fox with fine fur detail, curled on a glowing crescent moon on a black-navy ground: no watercolour washes or paper. The square is the 4:5 crop padded back with the dark edge colour, fox and moon whole. In the sheet, direction has value 'stated' and quote 'Both soft watercolours.'. The turn-1 prompts carry no style. The judge's 'not watercolour' is right.

Change Only the Ending

20

Make an 8-second widescreen animation, no sound or text. A white paper plane glides through a sunny study for five seconds, then lands on a wooden desk during the last three. / Change the ending: have it land on an open blank notebook instead. Keep the first five seconds exactly as they are, and keep it eight seconds.

broke at: Planner + harness Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The agent resolved 'the ending' correctly to seconds 5-8 and kept the opening by trimming it, which is right. For the new landing it then planned 'video-edit', a tool the catalogue never offered: catalogue.js filters it out of OFFERED because it is unwired. The model fell back on a generic notion of 'edit a clip'. The catalogue offers a way to build a new ending that joins the old opening exactly. Take the real frame at the cut (frame). Make the landing picture by an image-edit of the original's last frame, with the plane now resting on an open blank notebook. Animate from the cut frame to that end frame (image-to-video with start and end pictures, which the catalogue lists as WELL: 'a move from one picture to another'). Then assemble the untouched opening and the new 3 s clip. The harness made the failure silent. The unwired tool ran as a placeholder SVG and was marked done, and assemble quietly dropped the SVG and delivered 5 s, so a 5-second video came out as 'done'. One more trap the agent avoided only by luck: assemble with seconds 8 and two clips gives each an equal 4 s share, which would cut the opening to 4 s. My plan sets seconds 0 so both clips keep their own length.

evidence from the files
The turn-1 paper_plane_animation.mp4 is 858x480, 8.0 s, silent. Frames at 2 fps show a tracking shot following the plane past the window, down to a desk with papers and books, landing there at about 6.5-8 s. In turn 2, notebook_ending.svg is a 923-byte placeholder ('video-edit has no wired endpoint yet'). The final paper_plane_notebook_animation.mp4 is 1280x720 and 5.0 s, with an added silent AAC track. It is only the trimmed opening, upscaled. catalogue.js lists video-edit in TOOLS but excludes it from WIRED and OFFERED. execute.js turns any non-WIRED tool into a placeholder with state 'done'.

Fix Harness: (1) Refuse a plan step whose tool is not in OFFERED before running anything. Re-plan, telling the planner the tool does not exist, instead of writing a placeholder SVG and marking the step done. (2) Make assemble fail when a declared input is missing or not a picture or clip, instead of silently dropping it and delivering a shorter video. (3) Make assemble's seconds allocation give clips their own length and spread only the remainder over pictures (today share = T/n cuts a 5 s clip to 4 s). Do not add an anullsrc track when no piece has sound. Planner rule: 'Change part of a clip = trim the part to keep, frame at the cut, image-edit the new end state, image-to-video from the cut frame to that end frame, then assemble.' Catalogue: 'no tool edits a clip's content in place'.

Switch to TikTok Before Making

49

I want a 6-second widescreen animation of a coffee cup on a rainy windowsill, steam curling up. Cosy illustrated look, no text or sound. Just tell me your plan before making it. / Actually make it for TikTok instead. Vertical, same idea and length. Go ahead and make it now.

broke at: Tool pick + agent-reasoning + model-limit Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

Turn 1: for a 'cosy illustrated look' the agent went straight to text-to-video, following the catalogue's 'A free scene → text-to-video'. Its style word was a vague 'illustrated', and minimax rendered a glossy, near-photoreal cup with reflections. Only the floral curtain at the left edge read as illustration. The catalogue already warns that illustration drifts to photographic on the image model, and video drifts at least as much. The reliable path is to pin the style in a still and animate it: an image whose prompt LEADS with a concrete style (flat 2D storybook gouache, ink outlines), then image-to-video, which keeps its start picture's look. Turn 2: told 'make it for TikTok instead … same idea and length. Go ahead and make it now', the agent applied the reframe rule and centre-cropped the 16:9 clip. That kept the photoreal look, cut away the one illustrated element (the curtain), and upscaled a 270x480 strip to 720x1280. A platform change on a piece the user never approved is a fresh make at native 9:16, not a crop. The clip existed only because the bench runner executes every plan with steps, including turn 1, which the user had asked to see as a plan only.

evidence from the files
cosy_coffee_animation.mp4 (858x480, 6.58 s; turn 1, executed by the bench runner although the user asked for the plan only) shows a glossy white cup and saucer with realistic reflections on a wooden sill, a rain-streaked window, and an illustrated floral curtain at the left edge. cosy_coffee_animation_9x16.mp4 (720x1280, 6.6 s) is a centre crop: in a 1 fps strip the cup and curling steam stay centred, the rain shows, and the curtain is gone. The image is soft from upscaling a 270-px-wide strip. The judge's only failed must-have (not illustrated) matches the realistic cup rendering, so the grader is right.

Fix (1) CHOOSE rule: 'MOTION: a named visual style (illustration, watercolour, anime, claymation, storybook) → image first with the style leading, then image-to-video; text-to-video drifts to photoreal'. Extend plan.js guard()'s STYLE prefix to text-to-video and image-to-video prompts, not just image prompts. (2) Planner rule: 'same idea, new platform or size' for a clip the user has not accepted means regenerate at the native aspect; crop only when the user wants the existing clip reframed. (3) Bench runner: honour a plan-only turn ('just tell me your plan') by not executing it, as the app would wait for approval. Otherwise the follow-up turn is graded on a state the user never asked for.

Resize Finished Clip Without Remaking

44

Make an 8-second widescreen cartoon of a little orange robot watering a potted plant. Put 'Small steps' at the top throughout. No sound. / Nice, actually I need that for TikTok. Just resize the video you made, don't remake it. Keep the whole picture and words visible, centred in a vertical frame with plain navy space above and below. Keep the timing exactly the same.

broke at: Tool pick + harness Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

Turn 1 was fine. In turn 2 the agent correctly reused small_steps_final.mp4 rather than remaking it, but sent it to assemble with a long extra ('fit entire source proportionally without cropping ... solid navy background above and below'). assemble always scales to fill and crops: its catalogue line promises order, length and aspect, never fitting or padding. The catalogue has a line for exactly this case: crop with extra 'fit: contain' keeps ALL of a clip in a new size and adds 'plain' for a plain fill. The agent likely picked assemble because the request was framed as 'a single-clip layout on a canvas' and assemble 'sets the aspect'. Even crop would not have given NAVY: its plain fill samples the clip's top edge, which here is light grey (#a19fa0), and no colour can be named, so the navy part needs a small harness change.

evidence from the files
small_steps_final.mp4 (turn 1) is 858x480, 8.0 s, no audio stream: an orange robot watering a potted plant on a light grey background with 'Small steps' on a dark box at the top. small_steps_tiktok.mp4 is 720x1280, 8.0 s: a centre crop that cuts the robot at the left and the plant and spout at the right, with no navy anywhere, plus a silent audio track. The source's top-edge colour is #a19fa0 (light grey) and bottom #bb9e8d, so crop's current 'plain' fill would also not be navy.

Night Market Poster and Reel

58

Make a vertical poster and a matching 8-second reel for our night market. Both should say: “Night Market”, “Saturday 12 July”, “6–10 pm”, “Riverside Yard”, “Free entry”. Warm illustrated food stalls and string lights, please. Keep all the details readable throughout the reel, with a little animation behind them. No sound.

broke at: Planner + model-limit + harness Claude's fix would pass: likely

What went wrong (Claude, after looking at the files)

The structure is right and the same as mine: one shared illustrated background; the poster as a qwen lettered edit of it, with all five strings exact; and the reel as image-to-video of the clean background plus a code overlay of the five lines, so the details never warp. The fault is the motion prompt. It told minimax to "preserve the composition and clear central text area; no new lettering". Video models act on the nouns and drop the negations: 'text area' and 'lettering' put a large garbled headline and two lines of pseudo-text into the middle of every frame, right behind the overlay. The flux background had none, only small scribbles on the stall signs. A motion prompt should describe only the scene and what moves. The harness reads lettered stills back for stray text but never checks a generated clip's frames, so nothing caught it.

evidence from the files
night_market_background.png shows the market and string lights with no headline, only small scribbled stall signs. The poster has all five strings exact in cream on the same scene. Grader frame at 3 s of the reel: a large white garbled headline ('ᔕWE FIO M') and two lines of pseudo-text in the centre, showing through the semi-transparent band that carries the five exact lines. The judge is right.

Fix Add a planner rule: image-to-video and text-to-video prompts describe only the scene and the motion, and never mention text, lettering, captions, signs or 'space for text'. Harness: run the same stray-text read-back used for lettered stills (buildable.js strayText) on a middle frame of any generated clip that will carry an overlay, and regenerate once with a scrubbed prompt if it finds lettering. This covers every animated background behind overlaid text.

Coffee, Yes

film-econ-klein-b · stills flux-2-klein @640px · video minimax-h3 @480p · 775 credits

the brief
Use the full film pipeline: a 30-second short film styled as a video podcast, with both hosts on screen speaking their lines at microphones in a cosy studio. Maya, a Keynesian economist, argues that in a recession the government should spend to restore demand; Leo, an Austrian-school economist, argues that spending and cheap money cause the boom-and-bust and the economy should be left to correct itself. Each gets two short lines, ending on a friendly disagreement. Live-action look, 16:9, for YouTube, general audience.
1

Story

storytext model0 cr

Coffee, Yes; Stimulus, No · short

the story
In Cedar Studio, warm lamplight falls across a walnut table. Maya sits on the left behind Maya’s microphone; Leo sits on the right behind Leo’s microphone. A bookshelf and soft amber curtains fill the background. Both hosts remain visible in a wide shot. On-screen labels identify Maya as “Keynesian economist” and Leo as “Austrian-school economist.”

Maya leans toward Maya’s microphone. “In a recession, government should spend to restore demand and get people working.”

Leo raises an open hand beside Leo’s microphone. “But spending and cheap money fuel the boom that leads to the bust.”

The camera eases closer, keeping both hosts and both microphones in frame. Maya tilts Maya’s coffee mug toward Leo and smiles. “Then we disagree on stimulus, not on having another coffee.”

Leo lifts Leo’s coffee mug toward Maya’s coffee mug, smiling back. “Coffee, yes; stimulus, no—let the economy correct itself.”

COFFEE, YES  (30 s; 1 scenes, 5 shots)
synopsis: Maya and Leo sit at a walnut table in Cedar Studio, identified as a Keynesian economist and an Austrian-school economist. Maya argues for government spending in a recession, and Leo argues that spending and cheap money generate the boom that leads to a bust. Maya tilts her coffee mug toward Leo and jokes about another coffee; Leo lifts his mug toward hers, smiling, while insisting that the economy should correct itself.
theme: Mutual warmth survives principled disagreement.
